Naval base Den Helder conducts security exercise with reservists In November 2017, a security and protection exercise took place at naval base Den Helder. This was conducted for the first time with the deployment of over 100 reservists from the Royal Netherlands Navy. During the weekend, the South Gate of the naval base was open for New Year's during SAIL.

[SECTION BREAK]

6_KM_Annual_Report_2017_MATERIAL_MAINTENANCE-7 162 The Directorate of Material Maintenance opened and monitored reservists 24/7. The area behind the South Gate was also part of the training ground. There, patrols were conducted, an observation post was established, and a command post was located.

[SECTION BREAK]

Shooting Range (SSB) In addition to all regular and irregular requests for the shooting range (schools, MBV shooting, boarding teams, NLMARSOF), the International Shooting Competition for the Shooting Trophy took place at the end of the year. Besides the Dutch participation, many foreign teams also took part in this competition, and it was a great success again this year. FT&S At the beginning of each year, the first event on the agenda of the Sports Office is the New Year's Run/Dive. Subsequently, events followed in rapid succession. MK indoor football, NMK indoor football, 45+ Ron. v.d. Ham Memorial Badminton Tournament, MK Duathlon, the Triathlon in Biddinghuizen, the Port Run, Veterans indoor football, and MK field football. For all these events, the Sports Office MBDH is responsible for the organization and/or support. Additionally, military personnel who wanted to stay fit could once again rely on the gym, where, under the guidance of professional sports instructors, they could participate in lessons/training in boxing, circuit training, Cross Fit, Navy Fit, running training, spinning, and training for obtaining the NOC/NSF medal. Transport Despite the ever-increasing demand, the Transport Department also tried as much as possible in 2017 to support the operational activities.

This resulted in a considerable extra burden for the barracks and all available sports facilities. Thanks in part to all the challenges that arose, the staff, together with local supporters such as DBBO, PARESTO, and FBD, were able to demonstrate this year what the MEA can do and what significance it holds for CZSK, Defense, and the city of Amsterdam. Events in 2017 Right from the first week of January, the MEA operated at full capacity. The first conference was immediately one of the larger gatherings that took place this year in the event center. This was the NATO Maritime Operations Working Group. This conference had a special aspect; exceptionally, all partners of the conference participants were also accommodated at the barracks. A limited ladies' program also took place. Unfortunately, the participants of this MAROPSWG could not be motivated to join the annual New Year's run of the barracks, a sporting event where participation is more important than winning and where prizes are determined by lottery.

[SECTION BREAK]

This year, it was also noted that the number of visitors was nearly the same as in previous years. A total of 33,135 visitors were welcomed during 983 events and reservations. In addition to MAROPSWG, various large NATO conferences, symposia, and sports events were hosted, including the Military World Championship in Basketball. The barracks also served multiple times as the host location for the Admiralty Council, which conducted the three-day retreat at the MEA, during which the Sail Plan 2030 and the future of the Royal Netherlands Navy in general were discussed. This year, shared use of the conference facilities by civilian partners was again arranged by the Project Bureau Marine Terrain Amsterdam, but unfortunately, this was minimally utilized. Accommodation This year, over fifteen thousand reservations for Short-Term Accommodation were processed for activities at and around the MEA.

[SECTION BREAK]

In many cases, a port visit was made to Amsterdam as part of a transit, but also to a greater extent for deployment in support of national authorities. This year, several foreign units also visited Amsterdam, with the most notable being the Brazilian training ship NE Brasil.

Likewise, the sixth edition of the ‘Amsterdam City Swim’, the grand swimming event for fundraising to combat the disease ALS, took place. Colonel (ltkolmarns) J.P.C. ten Hove The Van Ghent Barracks has as its main task the provision of support to the Marine Training Center (MOC), the Royal Netherlands Navy Marine Band, the Fleet and Roadshow, and the Naval Barracks in Vlissingen. The Purple Restaurant Organization (ParestO), the Defense Facility Company (FBD), the Medical and Personnel Care Department (GPZ), and the National Real Estate Company (RvB) are fully integrated into the barracks organization. Additionally, the barracks plays an important role in events organized at and from the barracks. Examples include the World Port Days, various wreath-laying ceremonies, symposia, and the annual Rotterdam Veterans Day.

[SECTION BREAK]

The MOC is housed at the Van Ghent Barracks. The main training courses at the MOC are the First Military Training for Marines (EMV), the Corporals Training, and the Practical Training for Marine Officers (POTOM). Additionally, the practical weeks of Safety & Craftsmanship (VeVa) and various career and specialized function training courses take place. The barracks also plays an important role this year in organizing events.

Naval Base Vlissingen (MKVLIS) Commander: Lt. Commander (ltz1) H.W.M. Veldhuizen In 2017, there was no need for the main task, which is accommodating CZSK ship crews, just as in previous years. After Zr.Ms.

[SECTION BREAK]

Evertsen in 2015, no CZSK units have been in Vlissingen for maintenance or new construction, resulting in stagnation of the accommodation of ship crews. The fact that this task has not been fulfilled does not mean that the Naval Base Vlissingen (MKVLIS) has not experienced activities.

[SECTION BREAK]

In 2017, we again saw a shift in tasks towards a more general, facilitating character. As a result, the current two core tasks for the base in Vlissingen consist primarily of facilitating and supporting a large number of exercises for CZSK units and other military components. The second core task involves collaborating and networking with government agencies and the business community for the purpose of the new barracks to be built in 2021. The closing date of MKVLIS is April 1, 2018.

[SECTION BREAK]

6_KM_Annual_Report_2017_DIRECTORATE_MATERIAL_MAINTENANCE-16 171 Directorate of Material Maintenance This year, various units have been stationed at MK Vlissingen for battlefield tours. Among them were the Middelbare Defensie Vorming, several CLAS units, and the Atlantische Commissie Foundation. The VEVA training program set up its camp at MKVLIS for several weeks from mid-January to early March. The Marine Corps conducted a CERTIFEX exercise from the barracks both in the spring and in the autumn. The exercise area for the marines included not only the city center and beach of Vlissingen but also the Zeeland port area.

[SECTION BREAK]

A large, three-week certification exercise of the 400GNK (Medical Company of the CLAS) was supported in the autumn. Additionally, the barracks were busy throughout the year with theme days from the Veiligheidsregio Zeeland, meetings of various defense components, reunions (former cadets, COM, AVOM, BNMO, BOSS), and receptions. Marines during an exercise in the port area of Vlissingen.

On April 12, the Marine Barracks Vlissingen organized the 37th Round of Walcheren. Accompanied by the Royal Marechaussee, over 350 cyclists (military and civilian) participated in this cycling tour of approximately 90 km. The 50th birthday of the Commander MKVLIS was also celebrated in a fun way with colleagues. Additionally, for the crew of MKVLIS, the annual barbecue was held as a gesture of solidarity, and to conclude the year, a Christmas dinner was organized. The closing date of MK Vlissingen on April 1, 2018, remains unchanged. Preparations are in full swing to transfer the barracks to the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf in good consultation as the main user, which will be responsible for the realization of the Michiel Adriaanszoon de Ruyter Barracks (MARKAZ) in the coming years.

6_KM_Annual_Report_2017_MATERIAL_MAINTENANCE-18 173 Directorate of Material Maintenance (VBHKAZ). This was especially true as the Marines were prepared for the VJTF this year. After Hurricane Irma struck Sint Maarten in September, personnel and equipment were also deployed from Doorn to provide initial relief in the West.

Meanwhile, the numerous transport movements continued for the intensive training program of the OPE MARNS. The vehicles and containers of the units were accompanied on the exercise terrain by containers from the moving company and vans from contractors. The barrack buildings Fak Fak (non-commissioned officers) and Algiers (troops) received a facelift. The flooring was renewed, the walls were painted, the ceilings were replaced, and new lighting was installed. Several hundred colleagues temporarily moved to another barrack room for this purpose. Furniture and other goods were temporarily stored. A carousel of logistical movements within the barracks had to seamlessly align with the training and deployment program.

[SECTION BREAK]

The meeting rooms Norway, Assen, and De Punt were also refurbished and equipped with new furniture and MULAN computers with projectors. This also applied to the Congress Hall, which received an entirely new sound system. Pantries were built in building Sisophon. The Old Sick Bay and the Old Sick Room were converted into storage rooms and equipped with shower facilities. A shelter was constructed in the garden of the Gouden Bal. In building Chatham, twelve additional flexible workspaces were created. The classrooms were re-carpeted and furnished. During the winter leave, a temporary accommodation was set up in the parking lot between the Cafeteria and the Congress Hall, complete with locker rooms and fully furnished barrack rooms.

[SECTION BREAK]

Meanwhile, work continued diligently on the 'output specification' for the MARKAZ to be built in Vlissingen. Although the process is still on schedule for a move.

Valent-Groot On January 1, 2017, it was 60 years since the establishment of the Energy Distribution Company (EDB), then called the Electricity Distribution Company. This anniversary was celebrated on January 12 with employees and former employees at Fort Westoever, where the old EDB emergency power plant is located.

[SECTION BREAK]

Due to the shift from self-execution to outsourcing, the amount of work preparation increased. The municipality of Den Helder, the Royal Netherlands Navy, Housing Foundation Den Helder, Willemsoord bv, Port of Den Helder, NAM, HVC, and the Hoogheemraadschap Hollands

[SECTION BREAK]

On March 15, the Directorate of Materiel Maintenance Noorderkwartier signed the Letter of Intent for the Exploration of Sustainable Heat Supply in Den Helder to explore the possibilities for a sustainable heating network. For the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM), the head of the Maritime Support Department, Captain (ktz) R.J.A.M. Ramaekers, signed. This collaboration gives a good push to the municipality of Den Helder's goal of becoming an energy-neutral municipality by 2040. On October 1, the Combined Heat and Power Station, the energy plant at the Nieuwe Haven, celebrated its 25th anniversary. This was celebrated on September 26 at the station's premises with the employees of the EDB and their partners. Electricity consumption has grown 2.5 times in 25 years, but the objectives of the Combined Heat and Power Station remain the same as at the beginning: emergency power plant for the Defence locations in Den Helder, transformer station to provide ships with 60 Hz electricity and buildings with 50 Hz, as well as electricity production at times when consumption exceeds what the grid operator can supply. During the 3rd ‘Night of Military Music’ at the National Military Museum, there were presentations from various ensembles of the band. The first major ceremonial services with conductor Tien took place in Den Helder during the Assault of the KIM with a march through the position and a naval tattoo in celebration of King's Day. After the annual commemorations of May 4, the bombing of Rotterdam on May 14, and the CZSK commemoration in Den Helder, the group traveled to Chatham, 50 km southeast of London, at the beginning of June. Here, in the presence of, among others, Prince Maurits, extraordinary adjutant of the King, C-ZSK Lieutenant General of Marines, the Marine Band performed at the Van Ghent Barracks.

[SECTION BREAK]

Directorate of Material Maintenance R. Verkerk, First Sea Lord Admiral Sir Philip Jones, and together with the Band of HM’s Royal Marines from Portsmouth, commemorated the 350th anniversary of the famous Battle of Medway with a memorial ceremony, a tattoo, and two concerts. Back in the Netherlands, performances included appearances at the Naval Museum and during Navy Days in Den Helder, and with guest conductor H. Leenders at festivals in Sliedrecht and Zoetermeer. The next special performance took place on July 8 during the North Sea Jazz Festival. This was the first time a Dutch military orchestra played on the main stage of this festival in Rotterdam Ahoy, and with great success, trumpeter E. Training Vessels Naval Training Vessel Van Kinsbergen The ship primarily sailed for the KIM to train the cadets for the Naval Service. Additionally, it operated for the DVS and the MIWB in Terschelling. The ship had the following sailing periods. The year began with the first Sea practicals for the cadets from January 23 to February 19. During these weeks, the ship was in Kiel on Sundays and in Aalborg during the week.

[SECTION BREAK]

The second period involved training the non-commissioned officers for ZWST-K, from March 13 to March 20.

[SECTION BREAK]

The vessel visited the port of Aarhus during the week. The third sailing period was the second practical period for the cadets. This was from April 3 to April 30. On Sundays, the ship was in Kiel, and during the week, the ship was in Copenhagen. From May 7 to June 1, the Van Kinsbergen was in Terschelling for two different periods and sailed with students from the MIWB. The last trip before the summer leave was again for the purpose of training cadets. During this trip, the ship made a large round trip through the Baltic Sea. The ship visited several ports there during that period. During the visit to Karlskrona, the cadets rowed against students from the Swedish equivalent of the KIM. In Finnish waters, a Finnish liaison officer was on board, and the cadets and crew visited the Finnish KIM. After the summer leave, the ship made two more trips. The first was from September 25 to October 7 as a resit period for the cadets and the ZWST-K training. During this period, the ship spent one day in Kiel, Flensburg, and Aarhus. The last period was from October 23 to November 25. During this time, the ship again sailed for the cadets during their third practical period. The vessel was in Kiel on Sundays and alternated between Odense, Fredericia, and Sonderborg during the week.

From May 7 to June 1, the Van Kinsbergen was in Terschelling for two different periods and sailed with students from the MIWB. The last trip before the summer leave was again for the purpose of training cadets. During this trip, the ship made a large round trip through the Baltic Sea. The ship visited several ports there during that period. During the visit to Karlskrona, the cadets rowed against students from the Swedish equivalent of the KIM. In Finnish waters, a Finnish liaison officer was on board, and the cadets and crew visited the Finnish KIM. After the summer leave, the ship made two more trips. The first was from September 25 to October 7 as a resit period for the cadets and the ZWST-K training. During this period, the ship spent one day in Kiel, Flensburg, and Aarhus. The last period was from October 23 to November 25. During this time, the ship again sailed for the cadets during their third practical period. The vessel was in Kiel on Sundays and alternated between Odense, Fredericia, and Sonderborg during the week.

6_KM_Annual_Report_2017_MATERIAL_MAINTENANCE-30 185 Directorate of Material Maintenance Zr.Ms. Urania Commander: LtCdr (ltz1) W.W. Wester After its annual maintenance at the Van der Hoeven shipyard, which was completed on February 8, further preparations for the 2017 sailing season could take place in Den Helder. After Seatrain Command also gave approval, the sailing season began with a training week for cadets in the Wadden Sea and North Sea. Aspects such as current, wind, and tide were central during this training week. Subsequently, the ship sailed to Rotterdam for the Race of the Classics for students. Cadets from the Royal Naval Institute (KIM) formed the crew for this race, during which the ship won the "Sprint Cup." In May and June, the ship also conducted navigation training, for which it sailed to the southern coast of Britain and the Channel Islands. Since this year marked the 350th anniversary of Michiel de Ruyter's famous raid on the Medway with the Dutch fleet, Zr.Ms. Urania, following in the footsteps of our former fleet guardian, repeated this voyage on June 8.

[SECTION BREAK]

However, it had to endure a rare June storm in the English Channel before it could begin its journey towards Chatham from the French coast. During the crossing of the Channel, Urania experienced some time with an unclear propeller, causing it to drift away from its course to clear its rigging.

[SECTION BREAK]

After the commemoration in Chatham, the ship sailed via London to the Netherlands to attend SAIL Den Helder. This was also a precursor to numerous festivals in the Baltic Sea. In July and August, the Tall Ship Races were on the agenda.

[SECTION BREAK]

These took the ship through Sweden deep into the Gulf of Finland. The return journey went via Lithuania to the final finish in Poland. The crew during this race consisted of Dutch, Belgian, Swedish, and German cadets. After a period of VIP trips from Enkhuizen, the year was once again concluded with the Race of the Classics for Young Professionals, in which "Young Defense" provided the crew. At the beginning of November, the ship was delivered in Drimmelen for its fourth and possibly last maintenance period at the Van der Hoeven shipyard.

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean General In 2017, CZMCARIB served as a training area for both maritime and land exercises and took action in the fight against illegal activities at sea. In the second half of the year, special military assistance was requested, which ultimately resulted in a CZMCARIB-wide support operation.

[SECTION BREAK]

On September 6, Hurricane Irma passed over the Leeward Islands of Sint Maarten, Saba, and Sint Eustatius. It left a trail of destruction, with the former island being the hardest hit. Training and Support A variety of exercises and training sessions took place in the Caribbean over the past year. These were aimed at maintaining the operational readiness of the own units, but also served as an ideal training location for CZSK, CLSK, and CLAS units or partners in the region. In addition to its own training, CZMCARIB also supported training for important strategic partners in the Caribbean; the United States and France. The CZMCARIB units also trained abroad: at the American Camp Lejeune (Military Operations in Urban Terrain) and in French Guiana and Martinique (unit cohesion training). The Fight Against Drugs Prompt action to ensure safety at sea and from the sea required continuous vigilance. CZMCARIB is a '24/7 organization' where the Operations Center of the Maritime Headquarters Caribbean is staffed 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

[SECTION BREAK]

2017 yielded several operational successes, resulting in approximately 7000 kg of contraband being removed from the trade market. Arrival of the station ship Zr.Ms. Van Amstel in Curaçao.

[SECTION BREAK]

text:
The most significant coordination of deployment was the emergency relief operation for the islands affected by Hurricane Irma in the Leeward Islands and Dominica. Additionally, the MHKC frequently acted as the Commander of Military Resources (CMM) for various military assistance requests from the local governments of the islands in the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. The execution of main task 3, support of civil authorities, has significantly increased in recent years at CZMCARIB, thereby supporting the vision of becoming the maritime and security partner in the Caribbean. Station Ships This year, four ships were placed under the command of C-ZMCARIB as SSCG. Throughout the year, Zr.Ms. Holland, Zr.Ms. Van Amstel, Zr.Ms. Zeeland, and Zr.Ms. Van Speijk carried out the various tasks of the SSCG within the command area of CZMCARIB. All units were equipped with an NH90 onboard helicopter, which acted as a force multiplier in the various operations.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Counter Drugs All station ships have patrolled for both the Caribbean Coast Guard (KWCARIB) and for CTG 4.4. Various successes were achieved in this regard. In cooperation with international units, CTG 4.4 removed approximately 7000 kg of contraband from the trade market in 2017. In the international operations, cooperation took place with various countries including the United States, France, Colombia, the United Kingdom, and the Dominican Republic. Hurricane Relief In preparation for the hurricane season, which runs from June 1 to November 30, the annual Hurricane Exercise was conducted by CZMCARIB in collaboration with local authorities in the Leeward Islands. The importance of this exercise was demonstrated by the subsequent passages of various hurricanes through the Caribbean Sea. On September 6, Hurricane Irma passed over the Leeward Islands, leaving a trail of destruction.

Additionally, Zr.Ms. Zeeland (including NH90), Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, and part of the Company in the West (CIDW) were made ready to provide assistance. Patrol of Marines a day after the hurricane in Sint Maarten.

Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied. The DASH-8 patrol aircraft from KWCARIB was also used for transport and reconnaissance tasks following the hurricane. This operation was characterized by a joint deployment of all units and personnel from CZMCARIB and KWCARIB, with additional deployment of units and resources from Defense in the Netherlands. The number of deployed military personnel at the peak was approximately 1000 pax.

[SECTION BREAK]

This military operation was carried out jointly with various Caribbean security partners and lasted until October 31, after which it was scaled down. Military assistance from CZMCARIB provided both soft and hard military support to the authorities of the countries and islands of the Kingdom on several occasions. Some examples include: the Curaçao Militia (CURMIL) was deployed several times in 2017 for crime fighting as part of Ta Basta Awor. In Aruba, 32 RSQN contributed to investigations by the Korps Politie Aruba (KPA) and the Recherche Samenwerkingsteam by providing search capacity. Engineers from CIDW supported the police in Curaçao several times in searching homes and properties as part of judicial investigations. CZMCARIB assisted the authorities in Sint Maarten in searching cells of the penitentiary institution for prohibited substances, mobile phones, and weapons.

text:
The year was also marked by the optimization of SAP M&F and the implementation of Assortimentsgewijs Werken in de West (AGWW).

[SECTION BREAK]

Finally, we further developed SharePoint CZMCARIB, which is now widely used within the CARIB organization. Finances As of January 1, the payment office CZMCARIB and several financial management tasks were formally transferred to the Financial Administration and Management Office (FABK) of the Facilities and Logistics division of the Defense Support Command. The reallocation of financial management tasks to the FABK meant that CZMCARIB no longer performs accounting tasks, prior oversight of intended expenditures, and accountability for invoice payments. Consequently, four positions with the military personnel assigned to them were transferred to the FABK. Due to an increasingly intensive use of SAP M&F, including Assortimentsgewijs werken and VAM, it became apparent that traditional budget positions were underperforming and there was an unbudgeted realization associated with the budget position linked to SAP M&F. In 2017, based on financial volume, approximately 8% of the total realization of CZMCARIB was made payable through SAP M&F. The emergency aid resulting from the passage of Hurricane Irma in the Windward Islands resulted in €0.8 million in unbudgeted items.

[SECTION BREAK]

These additional expenditures were submitted to the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations and subsequently reconciled with CZMCARIB. In total, the final realization of CZMCARIB amounted to €20.5 million, thus remaining within the allocated budget.

text:
A large part of the year, the company restaurant 'Lamunchi' was under renovation, which was completed in November. The restaurant meets the latest standards and techniques, ensuring it will serve well for years to come. This beautiful result was thanks to intensive and good cooperation between the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf, the works council (as initiator), and the Logistics Service Food (LDV) staff of MBPAR. Additionally, the new Rima pier was completed and gratefully put into use by the support ship Zr.Ms. Pelikaan and the various station ships. The return of the 'West Ship' to the base has also restored the old robust military appearance of Parera, with all military units centralized at the military locations on the island. As part of maintenance, painting work and replacement of air conditioning units took place. There was also a cleanup of the so-called 'peanut butter area', where this year, through auctions/sales, more clarity has been achieved. The area is now organized, and all objects have been identified.

[SECTION BREAK]

Support and Assistance For Parera, the autumn was largely focused on providing assistance to the Leeward Islands after Hurricane Irma. Curaçao served during this period as a logistical transit point between the Netherlands and the Leeward Islands. The capacity of Parera was maximally utilized, with the sleeping accommodations (regularly 204 beds and 40 (emergency) sleeping places in the sports hall) being fully occupied, requiring daily food supplies for the entire occupancy. In addition to preparing meals at the base itself, mobile field kitchens, with LDV personnel from MBPAR, were deployed on Sint Maarten to support the military troops there. The MB-

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean PAR personnel proudly reflects on the support provided for delivering emergency aid. Additionally, MBPAR supported events throughout the year such as King's Day, the KLM Marathon, Tech Triathlon, Christmas Eve celebration, and the Christmas Market at Landhuis Ascension. The latter is a grand Christmas market at the Landhuis on the western side of Curaçao. CZMCARIB also made itself visible on this side of the island and provided a beautiful Christmas event for the local population and its own personnel.

text: Accommodation The accommodation has a spacious capacity for sleeping places, of which more than half is allocated to the KL Company in the West. The remaining places are used by boarders/sleep-in personnel, visiting units, and business travelers. Throughout the year, the accommodation was occupied for more than 90%, and during the deployment for emergency aid to Sint Maarten, even above 100% by creating emergency sleeping accommodation in the Sports Hall. Finally, the barracks prepared this year for improvements to the E-welfare in the sleeping accommodations and day rooms.

text:
In 2018, the Rijksvastgoedbedrijf will begin with the Zr.Ms. Zeeland en route from Curaçao to Sint Maarten.

[SECTION BREAK]

Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied is working on the installation of a new internet cable that can deliver data speeds up to modern standards. Digital television, fast (data) communication, and online gaming are expected to take shape in 2018 for all guests at the base.

[SECTION BREAK]

FT&S Development & Recreation (O&O) Like in previous years, FT&S organized many activities outside of regular sports support. Examples include the KLM marathon, the MTB tours, the Kingdom Games, the indoor football tournament, the team-building sports day, and activities for children (such as the Sinterklaas celebration, children's parties at the swimming pool, and Halloween kids movie night). The sports conditions in Curaçao remain optimal with two sports halls (MKSUF and MBPAR) and a swimming pool. Additionally, the barracks leadership decided last year to add a climbing tower, which was a strong desire of a large part of the staff, allowing climbing skills to be well maintained in the Caribbean. Company Restaurant The renovation of the company restaurant took place this year and was completed to full satisfaction in November. The official opening will take place in early 2018.

[SECTION BREAK]

During the period when the restaurant was unavailable, meals were prepared from mobile Karcher units of the Defense Loan Organization near the longroom for onboard placers/overnighters from MBPAR. The LDV staff managed to provide a warm meal daily from these less than optimal circumstances that met the quality standards expected of a regular company restaurant. Administration In December, the Administration Office was merged with the Defense International Support Service Center (DCIOD) into a joint support point/one-stop shop as part of the "Reorganization International Support Caribbean" project. This optimizes the organization's service to employees and their families.

Arriëns Dwarshuis, from February 27 Major (majmarns) C. van Dinteren The Marine Barracks Suffisant (MKSUF) was responsible this year for the readiness of CURMIL, continued the initiated movement towards the professionalization of this unit, welcomed the establishment of the Training Center CARIB, executed its facilitating role for visiting training units, and remained responsible for carrying out the Social Formation Trajectory (SVT). The support for the emergency relief operation following hurricanes Irma, Jose, and Maria demanded the utmost from the barracks and its crew. MKSUF committed to supporting, transporting, and registering refugees at Hato Airport. The barracks also facilitated the accommodation of many hundreds of military personnel participating in the emergency relief efforts. Even during the re-deployment, MKSUF was the location used by units before flying back to the Netherlands.

[SECTION BREAK]

A large number of discussions regarding collegial networking were held at the barracks. Throughout the year, training units from the Netherlands found their way to the barracks; military personnel participated in the exercise Daktari, NLMARSOF, DDG, KWCARIB, the MOC, and the sniper training. Foreign units, such as a French unit from Martinique, were also accommodated and supported in their training.

[SECTION BREAK]

After a pre-selection (Pre-POTOC), two Aruban candidates who started in 2016 were allowed to travel to the Netherlands in the spring. In August, a candidate from Curaçao began at the MOC in Rotterdam.

Because working at CARMIL is not a lifetime employment, the intake and the EMV, quantitatively but especially qualitatively, must be sufficiently robust. Of the 128 candidates, 78 were selected after a fitness test, a medical examination, and a psychological assessment. 67 local boys started, and ultimately 47 candidates completed the first intensive part of the one-year training after 4 months, resulting in a dropout rate of less than 30%, before they began the MBO certified training in Security and Surveillance or the combat training.

The green and blue platoon CURMIL The CURMIL green platoon is the operationally deployable unit.

[SECTION BREAK]

The Ministry of Justice and Security frequently requests assistance from Defense in reducing crime on the island. Ta Basta Awor, loosely translated as "Now is Enough," is one of the operations carried out. At the end of 2017, the authority of CURMIL was expanded to include the ability to search vehicles. Not only crime, but also other tensions on the island, such as support for local security services during the December strikes, required additional deployment of CURMIL. The CURMIL deployment for humanitarian aid operations in Sint Maarten, Saba, Sint Eustatius, and Dominica was unique; for the first time, this unit was deployed in such an operation. Their contribution proved to be of great added value to the operation. These troops speak the language, understand the culture, and are the perfect intermediaries between the deployed units and the local population. Through various national and international training programs, CURMIL continuously worked on their readiness and further professionalization, culminating in their successful participation in the French 'Commando' training in Martinique for the first time. Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied 202 The Command of the Navy in the Caribbean contributed significantly to its visibility through national holidays and participation in various ceremonial tasks. Once a year, a personnel change takes place, and militia members and corporals transition from the green platoon to the blue platoon. This latter platoon, which has been trained in their initial military formation to guard and secure defense objects, is deployed at both the naval base Suffisant and the naval base Parera. The guarding and securing of defense locations in Curaçao by the CURMIL is a responsible task that requires a great deal of discipline and ongoing retraining and IBT training. Social Formation Trajectory (SVT) The SVT is a training trajectory of approximately five months. This trajectory is aimed at instilling a positive behavioral change in underprivileged youth who have, for various reasons, found themselves on the fringes of society.

[SECTION BREAK]

Despite positive discussions with the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture, and Sports in Curaçao and a project group in Amsterdam, the next phase was postponed for budgetary reasons. Marines train in Curaçao.

[SECTION BREAK]

7_KM_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-18 203 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Region postponed the SVT appearance to the second half of 2018. Safety and health MKSUF has placed safety high on the agenda, once again as OCC. In mid-2017, both the business emergency plan and the BHV plan were revised, and various enforcement inspections yielded a positive score. text:
Emergency Aid to Sint Maarten, Saba, and Sint Eustatius

The 32RSQN, including ARUMIL, provided emergency aid in September on the Windward Islands after Hurricane Irma.

[SECTION BREAK]

The unit was already stationed on the islands prior to the passage. The 32RSQN was therefore the first unit to provide both hard and soft military assistance. The 32RSQN undertook the following tasks: staffing emergency shelters before and after the passage; supporting prison security; conducting patrols and setting up checkpoints at vital intersections; securing the air and sea ports to facilitate the transport of both personnel and equipment. Ultimately, the 32RSQN was active in the area for two weeks, after which the Maritime Support Task Unit (MSTU) relieved them.

[SECTION BREAK]

French Commando Training in Martinique

It is an old tradition for units of the Royal Netherlands Navy Command Caribbean (CZMCARIB) to participate in French commando training in Martinique. This has been conducted in recent years under the name Unit Cohesion Training. The training maintains and strengthens the (strategic) partnership with the French armed forces in the Caribbean. Additionally, the participating units practiced: completing the French jungle training; validating personal physical and mental readiness; improving junior leadership at levels 2 and 3; validating the expeditionary mindset by operating in and under extreme conditions; and intensifying cooperation with the French headquarters in Martinique. The 3rd Troop, ARU, and CURMIL participated in the training. Prior to the start of the training, the 3rd Troop underwent an intensive preparation program and also completed the French and Dutch Jungle tests. The French commando training consists of three components: a jungle component, a maritime component, and the final exercise. Ultimately, 19 marines from the 3rd Troop and 10 ARUMIL participated.

Search Operation House (searching for weapons)

A mixed team of search-trained personnel and trackers (10 marines) searched a house in support of an investigation by the detective unit. The task was to find a weapon. The support ensured that the designated property was systematically, thoroughly, and quickly searched. Ultimately, no weapon was found, but the involvement of the search team minimized the burden on the local residents.

[SECTION BREAK]

Search Operation

In November, 32RSQN, together with ARUMIL, supported the KPA in an urgent search. It concerned a missing person. It was presumed that this individual was a victim of a crime. The 32RSQN provided search capacity that made it possible to search more quickly across different axes. Ultimately, the person was found deceased by the KPA after further investigation.

[SECTION BREAK]

Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied Search operation (containers) The 32nd Reconnaissance Squadron (32RSQN) searched five containers at the request of the KPA, in which narcotics were suspected to be hidden. A composite group of infantry engineers, trackers, and logistics personnel, including a mechanic and forklift drivers, carried out this search operation. During this operation, 300 kilograms of cocaine were found. This search was conducted on MS-KSAV to keep the action discreet.

[SECTION BREAK]

The group had the advantage of easily being able to rely on various resources from the barracks. Logistics and equipment For the deployment in Sint Maarten after Hurricane Irma, the LDV from MSKSAV provided a team to cook in the mobile field kitchen. Two teams from Aruba and Curaçao prepared meals daily for over 700 people in two mobile field kitchens.

[SECTION BREAK]

Inspections In 2017, significant progress was made in the area of Monitor Quality Material. The Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) provided assistance with, among others, Zr.Ms. Zeeland.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean area focused on inventory management, particularly in the area of weapons and ammunition. The audit did not take place this year due to humanitarian deployment following Hurricane Irma in Sint Maarten. The KKW inspection revealed that a number of weapons were no longer permitted to be used. These were urgently replaced with new material. Additionally, a HACCP audit took place in the area of LDV.

The observation skills of the Rotating Element are one of the capabilities that the security partners do not possess, but for which they have a significant need.

Beat the Marines

Commander: Lieutenant (ltz1) M.E. van der Eerden 
The year began with the annual maintenance period. Several major projects were undertaken to increase operational readiness and minimize the risk of malfunctions. The most notable was the replacement of all external cabling, which had suffered greatly due to Caribbean weather conditions.

[SECTION BREAK]

text: Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied SAP Operations The implementation of SAP operations was prioritized in 2017 with various supporting visits from colleagues of CZSK/BVIV. The foundation is still not fully in order, although clear improvements are noticeable. In 2018, a SAP evaluation is planned, from which conclusions will be drawn on how to improve operations. Zr.Ms. Pelikaan The support ship with transport capacity underwent a Scheduled Maintenance (BO) in the first period of the year, as usual. This was fully carried out alongside the Rima dock at MBPAR. This year, two major tasks were additionally performed, which could not be postponed until the Maintenance Program scheduled for 2020. The first project involved nearly completely overhauling the hydraulic crane. The second project was the replacement of all external cabling and fixtures. Both projects were completed satisfactorily within the set time and budget. FRISC CZMCARIB has ten FRISC vessels at its disposal. Additionally, there are four FRISCs for the CARIB in the Netherlands that required extensive maintenance from the supplier. At the end of 2017, two arrived, with the remainder arriving in early 2018. The availability of the FRISCs improved significantly compared to previous years. Unfortunately, Hurricane Irma damaged both FRISCs in Sint Maarten to such an extent that they require a lengthy repair process. Coast Guard CARIB KWCARIB has ten super Rigid Hulled Inflatable Boats (RHIB). They have reached the end of their technical lifespan and these vessels will be replaced by Metal Sharks.

Melaet For 2017, P&O advice CARIB adhered to the objective of P&O: to provide the organization with sufficient, well-qualified, and motivated personnel. Timely and active staffing policy, good consultation with line managers and P&O CZSK, and a critical view on qualifications have proven essential to place the right employee in the right position. A pair of reports from the Dutch Safety Board indicated that inadequate safety, i.e., the failure to organize a safe workplace, was the cause of two fatal accidents within defense.

[SECTION BREAK]

This did not go unnoticed at CZMCARIB either. This is evidenced by the decision to organize, in addition to the Safety Council CZMCARIB, which meets four times a year, a specific Theme Safety Council for Incidents biannually. This specific Council is entirely focused on the station ship Zr.Ms. Van Amstel in Curaçao.

7_KM_Annual_Report_2017_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-35 220 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean focused on learning from incidents. Additionally, it was assessed to what extent commanders and department heads actually implemented the established improvement measures. This gave learning from incidents a visible place within the CZMCARIB organization. Thus, structural attention was created for areas of improvement. Within the CZMCARIB Staff, the emphasis was on compliance with (Dutch and international) laws and regulations, implementing defense policy, support, and an assessment of hazardous materials in preparation for the deployment during Hurricane Irma, as well as inventorying operational risks and employing a (third-year HBO) intern to support commanders and department heads. Furthermore, several meetings took place with various ministries of the country of Curaçao. These meetings consistently addressed the lack of an installation capable of processing chemical waste in a responsible manner. At MBPAR, the focus was on two specific areas. Firstly, a new emergency response organization was established, and the emergency response plan and the Business Emergency Plan were completed in draft form.

[SECTION BREAK]

Additionally, MBPAR functioned as a waste collection point for other defense locations in the Caribbean. From here, Zr.Ms. Karel Doorman transported the collected chemical waste in four 20-foot containers and 10 pallets to the Netherlands. This waste was subsequently processed through the established structure there. MKSUF made significant progress in the area of safety and security regarding the storage of hazardous materials and munitions. Furthermore, 2017 was characterized for MKSUF by ongoing delays concerning the asbestos remediation of the obstacle course and the training location 'Operations in Urban Areas'. As a result, both training facilities have not been used for more than two and a half years, which heavily impacts operational output (training).

text:
Company Social Work (BMW) region CARIB Head: Lieutenant Commander (ltz1) H.J.H. Goetzee.

[SECTION BREAK]

The main tasks performed by Company Social Work (BMW) in the Caribbean region are assistance, services, reporting, support after traumatic events, and crisis intervention. For the CARIB region, BMW, together with Spiritual Care (GV), is responsible for notifying family members. BMW is available 24/7 for personnel and their families. Since June 1, BMW has been part of the Personnel Care Service Center (DC PZ) of the Defense Support Command. In 2017, BMW provided psychosocial assistance to employees and their families throughout the CARIB region. Unlike the regional offices in the Netherlands, there is often a need for long-term assistance in the Caribbean region. This is partly due to the unique situation of overseas placements and the inability to rely on alternatives such as General Social Work or other forms of civil assistance. In 2017, the department regularly conducted work visits to Bonaire, where the Royal Marechaussee (KMAR) is active, and to Sint Maarten, in order to be more accessible to personnel and their families on these islands.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean In the context of providing services to commanders, information and advisory reports have been prepared, and participation has taken place in the Social Medical Team of CZMCARIB and the Royal Marechaussee. Due to Hurricane Irma, there was a significant demand for the deployment of the BMW personnel from BMW CARIB starting in September. An additional BMW member supported from the Netherlands for several weeks. This year, BMW also focused on the initiative to better address issues related to relational violence.

[SECTION BREAK]

The department held an informational session for several teachers from local schools where many children of defense personnel are placed. The goal of this collaboration is to recognize signals at an earlier stage and provide support if necessary. In doing so, we adhere to the official guidelines provided by Dutch law and the Professional Association of Social Work Professionals.

[SECTION BREAK]

BMW was also involved in local veteran care. In Curaçao, the Veterans Care first meeting was held in Sint Maarten to coordinate assistance.

text:
The Ascencion Country House is one of the objects of Monument Care Curaçao.

[SECTION BREAK]

Therefore, this residence is always open to the public on the first Sunday of the month. This open day starts with an ecumenical church service of word and prayer in the chapel of the Ascencion Country House, led by the chaplain or pastor. The audience consists of military personnel and their families, veterans, local people, tourists, and guests. After the service, people can meet each other in a relaxed atmosphere while enjoying snacks and drinks. There is music, stalls with books, jewelry, souvenirs, art, driftwood, etc. And there is an opportunity to participate in a guided tour of the estate with information about the history of the Country House. The open house and church services are well attended throughout the year.

[SECTION BREAK]

Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied

Additionally, formation days are regularly held by the chaplains. This year, the stationed military personnel of the CIDW were welcomed and introduced to the island of Curaçao. The military personnel working on the station ship were also given the opportunity to participate in a formation day together. The CURMIL enjoyed several training days on Ascension, as did the EMV, PO-TOC trainees, and the students of the police and coast guard training.

[SECTION BREAK]

In May, a FLO conference took place. Over three days, the Chaplaincy Service reflected on the past, present, and future. Normally, military personnel attend the FLO conference in Beukbergen in the Netherlands, but not everyone was able to do so. Furthermore, a number of FLO participants reside in Curaçao. Therefore, this tailored conference for military personnel and their partners was offered locally. Landhuis Ascension is a place where people like to go for meetings, team-building sessions, or gatherings. It is also frequently used as a training location. Dutch and foreign units regularly set up a command post there in 2017 and transformed the parking lot and the immediate surroundings of the landhuis into a bivouac site with tents, trucks, and communication equipment. After the deployment of military personnel to Sint Maarten, debriefing meetings were held on Ascension to reflect on this special task together.

Sint Maarten

The Royal Marechaussee has over 150 personnel working on various islands in the Caribbean. Therefore, the humanist counselor regularly travels to the Windward Islands and Bonaire to visit the personnel there. He can also be found at the Marechaussee brigade in Suffisant.

[SECTION BREAK]

2017 will go down in history as the year when Irma ravaged Sint Maarten. Immediately after the storm, the chaplaincy was present on the island to assist affected military personnel and families. In September and October, many military personnel were deployed to Sint Maarten. The chaplaincy was also present for them, even providing stroopwafels during church services or reflection services. In Aruba and Curaçao, the evacuated families were supported, and the chaplaincy assisted colleagues with the intensive work.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Celebrations From May 16 to 28, ten ladies from this choir traveled to Lourdes. In total, there was a delegation from Aruba and Curaçao of 41 participants who joined the Dutch delegation and took part in the impressive pilgrimage.

Traditionally, the spiritual care organized the Christmas Eve celebration on December 24. Over 800 people came to the parade ground of the naval base Parera that evening to celebrate this beautiful event together. The children's choir Angelitos and the Sranan Rosoes provided the musical entertainment, and there was poeroet and kerststol. The spiritual caregivers, together with the soldiers of the naval base Parera, contributed to a traditional and unifying celebration. The engineers of CIDW 26 built a new nativity scene for this celebration. Country House Ascencion. (Source: Wikimedia)

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Force in the Caribbean Area Spiritual caregivers also participated in exercises. Exercises of the CIDW were faithfully attended, as well as those of CURMIL. The spiritual caregiver from Aruba participated in exercises such as the MOUT in the United States. On board Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, spiritual care was regularly present. Moreover, they frequently visited the various units; whether they were active at Parera or Suffisant, with the Coast Guard or with the brigade of the Marechaussee. In 2017, they participated in various events: Ride for the Roses, sports days, all hands, solidarity meals, barracks meetings, receptions, introduction days for newly assigned personnel, notification services, OPS briefings, Social-Medical Consultations, veterans' café, crisis interventions, KLM marathon, good causes committee, MSV, hospital visits at SEHOS, etc.

Defense Materiel Organization/Joint Information Provision Command (DMO/JIVC) Team Leader: Lieutenant (ltz2) T. van der Wereld During the first half of the year, an inventory was conducted in preparation for the transfer of various ICT services (internet and telephony) from the CZSK organization to DMO/JIVC. In the second half of 2017, testing of the equipment to be used in the future began. A prerequisite for connecting the Marine detachment in Sint Maarten to the defense network was the dismantling of a microwave link and connecting the location to the fiber optic network of a local provider.

With a doctor and six Medical Assistants (AMV) on Sint Maarten, one AMV on Saba, one AMV on St Eustatius, one AMV on Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, and a medical advisor with a medical staff officer in Curaçao, a large deployment occurred. Furthermore, a trauma doctor, a staff doctor, a BME, and two evacuation teams along with a HPG member were flown in from the Netherlands to support and ultimately relieve the EGB personnel. Soldiers practice administering an intravenous line in Curaçao.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean In April, exactly one year after the establishment of the EGB, the evaluation period ended and it was time to take stock. Despite the need for some minor adjustments, the EGB is performing well. By the end of the year, this had resulted in the awarding of a civil quality certificate (HKZ). The Medical Service is also innovating in operational areas. Following the deployment in Sint Maarten, it adapted its own emergency aid package. The materials that the Service needs during such a mission are now more flexible to deploy and better equipped for the type of assistance it must provide. The personnel are also enthusiastic about integrating with the operational units to improve collaboration and increase mutual awareness between both parties.

text: KIM Cross - 50th Edition Under ideal weather conditions, the 50th edition of the KIM Cross took place on February 27. The start was at the soccer field of the Helder soccer club in Den Helder. For the cadets, participation was mandatory, but for many defense participants, it has become a baseline measurement for assessing their fitness level.

Commemoration of the Battle of the Java Sea "All ships follow me!" Thus spoke Rear Admiral Karel Doorman. Near the bust of Doorman, in the garden of the KIM, the Battle of the Java Sea was also commemorated on February 27, which took place on that date in 1942 between an Allied task force under his command and the Imperial Japanese Navy under Rear Admiral Takeo Takagi.

[SECTION BREAK]

The Combined Striking Force of 14 Dutch, American, British, and Australian ships was defeated. The blow was particularly hard for the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM). In addition to Doorman, over 900 KM personnel lost their lives in the waters of Indonesia. KIM Cross 2017.

Defense Simulation Symposium The second Defense Simulation Symposium took place this year at the ship handling simulator of the KIM. During the symposium, an interested audience listened to presentations from key players in the field, various workshops were held, and among others, cadets participated in demonstrations. Furthermore, there was ample opportunity to experience the latest maritime simulators firsthand. This year, the focus of the symposium was on maritime operations. The previous Defense Simulation Symposium highlighted land operations, and at a future event, the focus will be on air operations. The symposium was intended for all defense personnel involved in simulation systems as part of the Training and Education within the Readiness Process.

[SECTION BREAK]

The following evening, they were able to put their learning into practice in the presence of their parents. The Marine Corps Band held a concert at the theater de Kampanje for the entire Corps of Cadets, their parents, and the staff of the KIM. The installation was the concluding event, after which they could return home for the first time. The Monday after the installation, the cadets departed for the Marines to the Van Ghent Barracks to follow the Practical Training to Officer of the Marines. The remaining cadets began their classes at the KIM. Assaut 2017 The Assaut is the gala ball of the Corps of Cadets, which is part of the cadets' curriculum. From start to finish, this celebration is organized by the cadets, and the KIM undergoes a true metamorphosis. This year's theme was: 'Once upon a time in the West'.

[SECTION BREAK]

Coast Guard Netherlands Captain (ktz) R.J. Blok MSc In 2017, the Coast Guard made several important decisions regarding the modernization of the organization as well as the manner in which it carried out regular Coast Guard tasks in the areas of service and enforcement. The (political) decision-making regarding the new MOC to be developed was completed on December 7 with the discussion of the letter to the House, formally launching the project.

[SECTION BREAK]

This decision-making process is an important step towards a modern and future-oriented Coast Guard that operates information-driven and is equipped for its tasks. Furthermore, steps have been taken in the development of the operational resources through the elaboration of the operational concept "Interception from a ship." An important step in this is the commencement of an acclimatization period for information-driven deployment of an enforcement team consisting of police, customs, and the Royal Marechaussee (Koninklijke Marechaussee). Preparations for the acquisition of two Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPV) including interceptors, to replace the existing ships, have started in close cooperation with the Rijksrederij. An investigation into the formation of the Coast Guard in relation to its current tasks and modernization led to a principle approval for the expansion of the Coast Guard's formation by 23 FTEs. The implementation of this expansion will take place in the coming years through a reorganization process.

[SECTION BREAK]

FOREWORD In your hands is the annual report of the Royal Netherlands Navy 2018. In this report, you can read about the deployments the Navy undertook during extensive international operations and exercises, as well as the actions taken by the shore organization to facilitate these deployments. The Navy once again made a significant impression during the Navy Days in Den Helder.

[SECTION BREAK]

Additionally, this year featured Velas Latinoamérica Curaçao, a unique celebration where several tall ships visited Willemstad. The Navy was also represented there. With many visitors, it was a great success and a wonderful opportunity to showcase what the Navy has to offer. The personnel underwent many new training programs and participated in (international) exercises. At the World Port Days in Rotterdam, the Navy was present with marines and ships to introduce visitors to the naval forces.

[SECTION BREAK]

We hope that this Yearbook will prove to be a useful reference work. Editorial Team Yearbooks Royal Netherlands Navy. Foreword by Commander (kltz) Rob Kramer, Commander of Naval Forces.

text:
the Royal Netherlands Navy has been expanded. The F&C department has fulfilled its tasks, which consist of supporting C-ZSK (Royal Netherlands Navy Command) by providing preparation, execution, progress, and quality of financial policy advice, compiling the budget, and establishing the expenditure program, executing financial management as well as contributing to information provision through management and steering reports and preparing the cash forecast quarterly, which also includes proposed measures to remain within the financial frameworks. The expenditures by C-ZSK (Article 2 of the defense budget) were higher in 2018 than initially allocated at the beginning of the year. This was mainly due to increased expenditures for maintenance, for which additional budget was allocated to C-ZSK. The Rutte-III cabinet has made additional resources available to increase the operational deployability and sustainability of the armed forces. For the support of the armed forces, a total of four hundred million has been invested across Defense until 2021 in the support of the armed forces. This will finance, among other things, the need for supply capacity at sea and also expand the capacity for mine countermeasures in the North Sea.

[SECTION BREAK]

The training capacity for

At CZSK (Royal Netherlands Navy Command), several projects turned out to be more expensive than anticipated, such as the maintenance of Zr.Ms. Rotterdam and a high number of unexpected breakdowns due to the aging fleet.

[SECTION BREAK]

In 2018, forty million euros were added to the budget because the Caribbean Coast Guard was included in the CZSK budget. This year, CZSK entered into significantly more obligations than in 2018. This was primarily due to higher expenditures. Additionally, obligations increased because Defense took over those of the Caribbean Coast Guard from the Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations. Furthermore, an agreement has been made for the coming years for the maintenance of the Dornier aircraft of the Coast Guard Netherlands.

text: As part of the effort to achieve more simplicity and effectiveness, a pilot project was initiated on October 1, 2017, to test the independent small purchases (ZKA) process for 'small items'. In this pilot, the threshold for a simplified ordering procedure was raised from 1,250 euros including VAT to 15,000 euros excluding VAT. The intention is to give commanders more flexibility and to enable quicker small purchases. Automation has also been further improved, partly by implementing more financial management with SAP but also by continuously enhancing SAP, for example, by supporting VAT settlement with SAP in 2018.

4_KM_Annual_Report_2018_DIRECTORATE_OF_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-4 23 Directorate of Personnel and Operations adjustments had to be made to the assignments of the operational units. In some cases, this led to the cancellation of assignments.

[SECTION BREAK]

In addition, further guidelines were received to optimally but clustered distribute the available operational personnel across the Major Surface Units (GBW). In 2017, the project Development of the Armed Forces (DOKM) was initiated, for which a project organization had already been established. For CZSK, DOKM involved the expansion of operational (combat) support. In the coming years, these expansions will be implemented and will lead to, among other things, the expansion of mine countermeasure capacity, the establishment of the Fleet Marine Squadron, and a second supply ship. These promising future prospects resulted in the growth of the CZSK organization.

[SECTION BREAK]

This made it more challenging to provide the organization with sufficiently motivated and well-trained personnel. To attract future civilian personnel, the 'Pool of 100' was introduced. Personnel who do not yet have a position but expect to within three years due to the aging within the Directorate of Maritime Maintenance (DMI) had temporary placement within this Pool.

[SECTION BREAK]

This allowed them to participate in the application process from within the organization. Career Guidance Career guidance explored future possibilities together with the employee based on personal wishes and what the organization had to offer in terms of positions. This exploration took place in the form of a career conversation that is held during each position, or once every three years. This conversation encompassed personal developments and wishes for the near future. This personal development of the employee was necessary to keep them valuable to the organization. In addition to internal mobility, the career counselor paid attention to external mobility for employees who will not progress in the long term but will leave Defense. The career guidance section consists of four military offices for the service groups, namely the operational service, marines, technical service, and logistics service, and an office for civilian personnel. At the beginning of the year, this section had 37 military and three civilian positions. Career guidance for civilian personnel had been in place for over a year. The evaluation of this new phenomenon is currently ongoing and will be completed in 2019.

4_Navy_Annual_Report_2018_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-5 24 Directorate Personnel and Operations This year, various groups experienced personnel shortages. This was particularly evident among the junior officers and the middle management of the non-commissioned officers. Another concluded measure for personnel retention was that the constant shifting of personnel was minimized. An excessive number of first lieutenants of the Marines and corporals of the Technical Department was maintained to ultimately fill the scarcity in higher ranks.

[SECTION BREAK]

Royal Netherlands Navy Reserve The deployment of reservists has increased due to the introduction of the Adaptive Armed Forces. This led to a desired growth of the Royal Netherlands Navy Reserve and further professionalization. In 2018, the number of reservists grew by more than two hundred individuals. These were not only former colleagues but also people without prior military experience.

[SECTION BREAK]

This also meant that the hours of deployment increased compared to 2017. These reservists were appointed due to their accumulated experience in the civilian world and their specific expertise. A portion of this new intake joined the Navy through the Defensity College program. In this program, students are given the opportunity to work for one or two days a week during their bachelor’s and master’s studies for the Zr.Ms. De Zeven Provinciën undergoing maintenance at the DMI in Den Helder.

[SECTION BREAK]

25 Directorate of Personnel and Operations Management They are appointed as aspirant officers in the reserves. During their studies, they are trained as officers through military and additional training in leadership. After completing their studies, they choose to continue their career as reserve officers or to receive further training to become career officers. Bureau Flexible Capacity During the previous year, the Bureau Flexible Capacity was established to gain more control over the deployment of flexible personnel. This referred to reservists, civilians, and temporarily available military personnel. In 2018, this bureau was further expanded with the introduction of a recruitment pool for civilian personnel. Bureau Flexible Capacity was a successful instrument that provided the organization with more insight into the need for flexible personnel and their expertise.

This gives an impulse to the OKM vision towards place and time-independent learning. The Training Center CARIB was supported in setting up the guidance structure. Educational personnel from OC Carib were qualified according to learning line 2 of the ECOD (remotely). Contributions from OKM to the Sprints of the defense-wide project Quality in Image (KIB) have ensured visible recognition and acknowledgment of OKM qualifications within the civilian world. The DOKM project has created opportunities to attract various new educational staff to the OKM schools. These were often veterans, which has the advantage that they are familiar with the context. This also provided the opportunity to attract educationally or training-qualified personnel, which resulted in a quality boost. 4_KM_Annual_Report_2018_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-17 36 Directorate Personnel and Operations Defense Diving Group & Defense Diving School (DDG & DDS) Commander: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) B.A. Visser, from September 7 Lieutenant Colonel (ltkolmarns) E. Hofma DDS The DDS is part of the Defense Diving Group (DDG). This organization is led by the Commander of the Defense Diving Group (C-DDG), who also serves as the Commander of the DDS (C-DDS). The C-DDG/C-DDS sets the standards and oversees not only the operations and staff division of the DDG (red) but also the training process (blue). The certification institution, knowledge and quality bureau (CIKK) acts as the standard bearer and reports directly to H-OKM. The objective of the DDS is to safely and timely provide training, certifications, refreshers, and exercises in the areas of working under pressure, subsurface search, mine countermeasure diving, maritime special forces operations, maritime demolition, maritime explosive ordnance disposal (EOD), and maritime improvised explosive device (IED) operations. DDG In 2018, the DDG was heavily involved in national operations. Various preventive search operations for Host Nation Support were carried out. Additionally, several search assignments for police and justice were completed.

[SECTION BREAK]

In June, the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) published an internal report on the fatal diving accident in 2015 in Curaçao. With a letter to Parliament, the Minister informed the House of Representatives how she intends to increase diving safety following this incident. After its publication, all diving operations were suspended for a week to update personnel on the investigation, the recommendations, and the measures, and to actively reflect on the safety awareness of the unit.

Various employees pursued different technical vocational and/or functional training at various points in their careers, both in groups and individually. This ranged from one-day to long-term training.

As part of international collaborations, the KMTO also trained foreign naval colleagues. For example, Chilean colleagues attended the Technical Central (TC) Procedures MF module at the KMTO. German colleagues underwent training for the APAR radar, and employees from Belgium participated in Functional Education and the System Responsible Officer (SVO) training.

[SECTION BREAK]

The KMTO had a total of 71 foreign students last year. Instructors and educational development teams attended courses from the Defense Training Expertise Center (ECOD) to maintain their skills at the appropriate level. This made Defense as an organization more agile at lower costs with higher quality.

Dutch-Belgian Operational School (NLBEOPS) Commander: kvk C.D.P. Colonval, from June 27 kltz E.J. Horstman The year was very eventful and full of challenges for NLBEOPS in terms of personnel and equipment. In addition to realizing the training plans, the goal was to secure the staffing and sustainability of NLBEOPS. At the beginning of the year, a new class of cadets was installed at the KIM in Den Helder.

[SECTION BREAK]

4_KM_Annual_Report_2018_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-22 41 Directorate Personnel and Operations NLBEOPS was 100% filled, in some cases directive. Throughout the year, it became clear that the occupancy rate would significantly decrease. As a result, discussions were held with Personnel and Organization (P&O) and Training Royal Netherlands Navy (OKM). Since personnel filling is a Navy-wide issue, this ultimately resulted in a prioritization issued by the Commander Royal Netherlands Navy (C-ZSK). In terms of personnel, eight positions were created based on budget obtained through the Second Chamber motion by Van der Staaij. Two commanding officers for the Safety and Craftsmanship (VeVa) vessels were hired, and a position was created for a maritime psychologist. This year, a multimedia staff member was also added to the personnel of NLBEOPS. This has already led to innovation and modernization in various aspects of the provided education. Several initiatives were realized to improve education. For instance, the maritime English cell, led by the Defense Language Center, developed vocational-oriented English.

Opening of the Seamanship Trainer On February 21, the ceremonial opening of the Seamanship Trainer (ZMST) took place, conducted by C-ZSK Vice Admiral Kramer. This occurred in the presence of Captain (ktz) N. Delfos, former commander of the replenishment tanker Hr.Ms. Poolster, the unit after which the Seamanship Trainer (ZMST) is named. After the opening, several larger outstanding issues were addressed by the contractor. Subsequently, the trainer was put into use on April 18 for training the Dutch and Belgian EVO and Voortgezette Vakopleiding (VVO). Additionally, it was also used for VeVa students and the EMMV for general shipwrecks and team training for the crew of units. This is a unique trainer in the Netherlands to prepare personnel for various nautical operations, such as at-sea replenishment and anchoring. Until now, this could only be done in the United Kingdom or the United States.

[SECTION BREAK]

ISO Certification of Royal Netherlands Navy Training Throughout 2018, all OKM schools adjusted their internal operations to comply with the ISO 9001:2015 standard. Because this was coordinated closely with Sturing Beheersing & Coördinatie (SBC), the entire OKM organization was successfully certified by the Dutch Certification Institute.

[SECTION BREAK]

However, not all training courses are organized according to the BGO. Within NLBEOPS, there are a number of training courses that are, but others still need to be converted. Defense Sailing School (DVS) The year started well with the opening of the ZMST on February 21. The range of training was expanded with the ZMST, resulting in an increased presence of students on the Harssens peninsula.

[SECTION BREAK]

In contrast, the closure of the Dependence for daily operations took place. This decision was necessary due to the condition of the building. The personnel were temporarily housed with the other DVS personnel in the 'Klooster' at the KIM. Additionally, steps were taken to ensure that the planned new construction would not face further delays. Fortunately, the closure had only a minimal impact on the training, allowing all courses to proceed.

[SECTION BREAK]

The seamanship training unit conducted three EVO ODND courses in 2018, including an upgraded and a retraining variant, as well as a VVO ODND, which completed their BOZ training at the ZMST for the first time. Furthermore, many rubber boat, Rigid Hulled Inflatable Boat (RHIB), and crane training sessions were conducted. The navigation training unit provided, in addition to the regular training, four Navigation Modules <500 tons, a ZWST-K training, and a NATO GBW training last year. Due to low enrollment, the NATO Small Surface Units (KBW) course was canceled in 2018. The execution of the NATO GBW training was not without its challenges. After the required ships for practical sailing were unavailable in the first week, it was decided to halt the training. The amphibious sailing training was conducted by the training unit of the SSTG on Texel. They provided five LCRM, five Fast Raiding Interception and Special Forces Craft (FRISC), three LC BASIC, two LC3, and one LC2 training courses.

After the required ships for practical sailing were unavailable in the first week, it was decided to halt the training. The amphibious sailing training was conducted by the training unit of the SSTG on Texel. They provided five LCRM, five Fast Raiding Interception and Special Forces Craft (FRISC), three LC BASIC, two LC3, and one LC2 training courses.

Belgian-Dutch Mine Countermeasures School EGUERMIN Dutch leadership: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) M.M. Lambregts. The mine countermeasures school EGUERMIN is the training center for operational training and specific technical aspects for the minehunters of the Netherlands and Belgium. The training and courses provided are tailored in consultation with the Head of Training Royal Netherlands Navy (HOKM), the Competence Center of the Navy Component (CCMAR), and the NLMARFOR Sea Training Command according to the wishes of the Commander Royal Netherlands Navy and the Commander of the Belgian Navy Component.

[SECTION BREAK]

4_KM_Annual_Report_2018_DIRECTORATE_OF_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-27 46 Directorate of Personnel and Operations Binational training and exercises The crews of the Belgian and Dutch mine countermeasure units go to EGUERMIN to follow functional training: Enlisted personnel and non-commissioned officers from the Operational Service and naval officers learn to use various systems to detect and clear naval mines; Personnel from the Technical Service receive instruction on, among other things, the Degaussing System, which reduces the magnetic signature of the ships; Divers receive training on deck work and the operation of naval mines; Personnel responsible for deploying the Remote Environmental Monitoring Unit System (REMUS) Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) are trained at EGUERMIN to become REMUS 100 AUV Operators; Team training takes place in the TTF (Team Training Facility). The Marine Training Center in Rotterdam (MOC) Commander: Lieutenant Colonel (ltkolmarns) X.E. van den Berg, from July 1 Lieutenant Colonel (ltkolmarns) P.

[SECTION BREAK]

Damen The past year was busy with personnel changes, promotions, service time gratifications, and colleagues leaving the service. For the Marine Training Center, it was a year with three command transfers and a variety of training programs. It was also the year in which the task was assigned to revise the initial training and increase the recruitment assignment. This led to the 'charcoal sketch', which transitioned to four intakes and a split between the Basic Military Training (EMV) and EVO.

[SECTION BREAK]

This plan was developed in 2018 and presented in the AR. During the 440th meeting of the AR, the actual assignment was given to implement this plan starting in 2019.

This year, the various training departments accomplished a lot of work. A total of 164 marines were delivered, 166 students completed their VeVa, the career training department delivered 11 midshipmen and 77 corporals. Additionally, eight sergeants and corporals were offered the sergeant training, and three cadre members were given the Commander Raiding Section training. The sports training program trained 15 cadre members. Besides these training programs, various support activities were carried out. Furthermore, there were several nice events, such as the annual performance of the Marine Band and the pub quiz at the beginning of the year. The joint sports day was held after the summer break, and the year concluded with the Corps anniversary and the accompanying Boxing Gala.

[SECTION BREAK]

4_KM_Annual_Report_2018_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-28 47 Directorate Personnel and Operations There was nothing to complain about regarding attention to the Marine Training Center (MOC) last year. The Minister of Defence visited on January 18 and Knight of the Military William Order Major Marco Kroon visited on February 18. Additionally, the IGK, PC-ZSK, C-KIM, and DPBV were present at the events.

[SECTION BREAK]

A memorable moment for 2018 was that on January 22, the first female student started at the EMV. Finally, there was also a lot of activity concerning educational development and support for various Qualification Profiles. These were important for developing quality education and often brought discussions and emotions with them. Documents that were initiated this year will continue into the future, while the need to provide specific education already started in 2018. In addition to providing and supporting educational development, the first steps were also taken to give shape to the project Learning Environment of the Future from OKM.

[SECTION BREAK]

The MOC was the driving force behind this project, which aimed to embody the credo 'learn anytime and anywhere.'
