text:
Schelkers The JUZA department is part of the DP&O, one of the five line directorates of the CZSK. The department advises and supports CZSK, the directors of CZSK, and commanders of units on all legal issues that arise. JUZA provides legal advice and acts as a point of contact for the directors and commanders within the CZSK. Additionally, JUZA monitors the legal and administrative diligence of the operations within the CZSK. The main areas of law that the department deals with include (military) criminal and disciplinary law, operational law, and constitutional and administrative law. These areas of law are organized into three different bureaus.

[SECTION BREAK]

This allows every employee at JUZA to function as the first point of contact (counter function) for questions directed to the department. Therefore, JUZA does not provide legal advice to individual military personnel but does assist them if necessary. In criminal or disciplinary matters, JUZA is primarily involved on the side of CZSK and the Ministry of Defence as an organization. Should a military member be involved in a criminal case, they can receive assistance from the Ministry of Defence in this matter. Personnel and Organization (P&O) Head: Captain (ktz) E.C.W. Jansen, from May 2 Captain (ktz) N.W.B. Kempers P&O contributes as an expert Human Resource partner to the realization of CZSK's ambitions in the area of personnel readiness and good employment practices. The

[SECTION BREAK]

The Personnel and Organization Directorate achieves this by providing personnel with the opportunity to develop and grow. In this way, P&O, as a career development organization, makes a relevant contribution to Defense and the labor market. By engaging and inspiring employees, the possibility for flexible deployment in the future is created, allowing room for (innovative) initiatives.

All of this aims to ensure that CZSK (Royal Netherlands Navy Command) always has sufficient, well-qualified, and well-motivated personnel available to carry out its tasks. The P&O department has the following main tasks: providing P&O advice to C-ZSK regarding the functioning of the personnel function area, the organization and staffing, and the resulting required personnel readiness within CZSK; providing P&O advice to line management, commanders, and heads of service units, thereby achieving a uniform, consistent, and coherent implementation of personnel policy within the given frameworks; organizing and executing management development up to the level of Lieutenant Commander (kltz)/Lieutenant Colonel (ltkol)/scale 13, in conjunction with and aligned to the Management Development (MD) policy for the levels of Captain (ktz)/scale 14 and higher; organizing and executing the job allocation process and personnel management for military personnel within the frameworks of the Flexible Personnel System (FPS); The United Kingdom Carrier Strike Group viewed from Zr.Ms. Evertsen.

Medical and Personnel Care (GPZ) Head: Captain (ktz) (TA) B. van den Heuvel The GPZ oversees the entire medical service of CZSK.

[SECTION BREAK]

This oversight is often carried out through the heads of medical teams or officers responsible for the medical service. The head of GPZ also provides functional leadership to the medical service on ships operating in the Caribbean and to medical units within the Marines. The GPZ staff implements policy developments in collaboration with the executive management departments.

[SECTION BREAK]

Personnel and Organization Directorate Royal Netherlands Navy (OKM) Head: Colonel (ltkolmarns) S.J.C. Nommensen Bureau for Training Needs Assessment & Evaluation (OB&E) The year 2021 primarily consisted of executing regular tasks. OB&E manages the Continuous Workplace Qualification List (AKL) on behalf of the Competent Authority. The AKL is a Cognos overview from Peoplesoft that shows which (required or desired) qualifications are linked to the workplaces or function codes within CZSK. This list stems from the operations of the Authorities and is regularly updated. OB&E monitors the execution of the training and qualification needs assessment process (based on a new or changed task). This varies from creating a digital qualification need, assigning development tasks, monitoring progress, and evaluating Training and Individual Training (O&iT) proposals to creating O&T scripts and generally supporting the O&iT process in accordance with the defense-wide O&iT chain. Furthermore, OB&E provides a quarterly overview with the corresponding appreciation of individual Personnel Readiness regarding the CZSK safety qualifications for the Safety Council DP&O.

[SECTION BREAK]

Maritime Simulation Center (SimCenMar) In 2021, the department added three permanent positions for Media Design staff. This way, SimCenMar can be a recognized training company for interns and can continue the XR-campus concept with its flexible pool of employees. The same XR-campus moved in the autumn to the Maritime Emerging Technologies Innovation Park and is part of the Regional Deal Kop van Noord-Holland.

text:
The documents include a flowchart and a Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed table. Some examples of applicable (numbered) OKM working instructions are 'executing O&iT', 'submitting exemptions', 'dyslexia', 'exemption at own request', and so on. The purpose of the working instructions is to provide the OKM schools with guidelines for organizing the main process of executing O&iT activities. To continue to provide a lasting impetus to the OKM vision and to enable location- and time-independent learning, the company Gamified Peer to Peer Adaptive Learning (GPAL) has been offering opportunities for digital and remote learning since 2015. There is now a management and development environment and an Android & IOS app with video (learning) modules available. The functional and technical management is assigned to the Joint Information Provision Command (JIVC). To meet the security requirements of Defense, JIVC executed the task of integrating GPAL into the Mobile Device Management environment of Mulan. OWZ coordinates with JIVC regarding the creation of desired projects and provides a representative or contact person for the periodic GPAL coordinators' meeting. OWZ supports the Caribbean Training Center (OCC), starting from February 2020, in establishing the guidance structure. In this regard, the department remotely qualifies the teaching staff of OCC based on existing learning lines from the Defense Expertise Center for Training.

[SECTION BREAK]

Safety and craftsmanship (VeVa) Within VeVa, CZSK has five directions: Maritime, Mechatronics, Ground Operations, Commercial Vehicle Technology, and Aircraft Maintenance Technology. For the vocational directions Maritime, Mechatronics, and Ground Operations, there are two levels at the KM: MBO2 and MBO3. For Aircraft Maintenance, there is level 4, while Commercial Vehicle Technology only has level 2. The three levels are for sailor/marine N2 and for aspiring corporal N3 & N4. Four schools are responsible for the Vocational Practical Training (BPV), namely SMVBO, KMTO, NLBEOPS, and MOC.

M. Flaman EMSD The motto of KMTO is: “We train maritime technicians.” This institution provides vocational and functional education for the personnel of the Technical Service (TD), but also for the (technical) personnel of other services and defense components. Additionally, the school makes an important contribution to the training and development of crews of operational units, both above and below water. For training and development purposes, KMTO has representative practical resources and simulators. Students All new sailors and non-commissioned officers of the TD of the navy begin their careers at KMTO. In 2021, 28 sailors started with the EVO and 46 with the First Adjustment Module. Additionally, twelve non-commissioned officers, who had already gained operational experience as sailors, began their technical MBO4 training in Service and Maintenance at ROC Kop van Noord-Holland. Besides the 'regular' entrants, there are also VeVa students. KMTO collaborates with ROCs spread throughout the country, which provide the VeVa training with the specialization in Mechatronics level 2 and 3. The VeVa students follow their vocational education at the ROCs and receive practical training (BPV) at KMTO during their education. In 2021, 46 VeVa students started this training at the school.

text:
In addition to the new intake, KMTO provides education for the already serving technical personnel. Various employees follow different technical vocational and/or functional training courses at various times in their careers, both in groups and individually, ranging from one-day to long-term courses. Through international collaborations, KMTO also trains foreign naval colleagues.

[SECTION BREAK]

Due to travel restrictions related to the pandemic, the number of foreign students this year was significantly smaller than in the years before COVID-19. In 2021, lessons were still held for three Belgian colleagues. Impact of COVID-19 on activities Just like the previous year, the pandemic also influenced the activities of KMTO in 2021.

[SECTION BREAK]

By adhering to some basic principles, it was possible to continue (almost) all training safely. Within KMTO, the following three basic principles were applied: (1) Lessons that could take place remotely were conducted

[SECTION BREAK]

4_KM_Annual_Report_2021_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-16 37 Directorate of Personnel and Organization conducted distance education; (2) Practical lessons requiring in-person instruction took place on location within the RIVM guidelines; (3) If compliance with the RIVM guidelines during in-person instruction was impossible, these lessons only occurred after a task-risk analysis assessed the necessity against the risks. For all lessons requiring in-person instruction, procedures were established that described which specific measures were applicable to that particular lesson. Due to the school providing lessons in an adjusted format or because, due to COVID measures, fewer practical locations were available on the ships, the duration of the training sometimes became longer than before COVID. Developments and Innovation The management of KMTO noted in 2020 that the intake of sailors had stagnated in the previous years and that the market forecast indicated this was a structural trend. Additionally, the training pathway to sailor and corporal TD was perceived by the students as too long and too theoretical.

[SECTION BREAK]

To address these issues, the management of KMTO developed a plan for the Technical Vocational School CZSK in 2020, which significantly restructured the training approach. In 2021, the AR was tasked with realizing this plan. Collaboration was sought with all maritime schools in the Netherlands.

4_KM_Annual_Report_2021_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-17 38 Directorate Personnel and Organization of the qualification track Marine Technician, where school leavers with at least a VMBO diploma first follow two years of training as Maritime Officer All Ships at the maritime schools. During these two years, there are also several internship weeks with the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) where the students are taught navy-specific knowledge and get acquainted with working and living in the naval forces. After the first two years, when the students have reached adulthood, they enlist as military personnel to be trained as a corporal in technical service during the last two years in the rank of sailor. The principle during these last two years is: "on board where possible, at school where necessary." Throughout 2021, efforts were made to develop the curriculum so that the first class of students can start in September 2022. To provide practical lessons at KMTO for the Integrated Platform Management System and in the various forms as present in the fleet, the department delivered the new Integrated Platform Management System trainer in November. While the various subsystems are spread throughout the ship, they are located close together here, making it possible to provide effective practical education on this system.

[SECTION BREAK]

Personnel and organization The number of vacancies remained significantly high in 2021, making it necessary to cancel a considerable number of training courses. Although this meant that no technical personnel could be trained for some weapon systems, it was essential to keep the workload for the instructors at an acceptable level. Furthermore, it was not always possible to provide specific lessons because the necessary knowledge was lacking at the school due to the vacancies. There was also a backlog in educational development due to the large number of vacancies. Upskilling and training An important aspect within KMTO is the connection of technical training to operational management. It is important that the school maintains a link with practical work. In addition to the ship visits that are conducted in this context and the training that takes place on board, KMTO also regularly supports the upskilling unit of Sea Training Command (STC) with preparing the naval vessels for mission-specific readiness, sailing readiness, and exercise readiness.

4_KM_Annual_Report_2021_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-18 39 Directorate Personnel and Organization Dutch-Belgian Operational School (NLBEOPS) Commander: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) E.J. Horstman EMSD The year was once again a year full of challenges for NLBEOPS, especially due to the pandemic. The school had already established a robust organization in 2020, which allowed the staff to quickly anticipate the frequent COVID-19 waves this year. The training was adjusted multiple times to the prevailing circumstances and medical challenges. Thanks to good logistical support, internal operations could be maintained. Through the prevailing measures and the consistent use of self-tests, the school significantly reduced the risk of internal infection. A combination of flu-like symptoms and COVID-19 still led to some peaks in temporary staff absence and the necessity to adjust micro-planning. Each department critically and pragmatically assessed operations in relation to teleworking/remote working and the healthy work/life balance.

[SECTION BREAK]

The personnel filling of NLBEOPS was approximately 85%. The largest personnel shortages were present in the VeVa department, at the Defense Navigation School (DVS), and Above Water Warfare. The personnel situation gradually improved at VeVa. An additional burden for NLBEOPS was the necessary assignment of personnel for deployments and support of the fleet.

[SECTION BREAK]

Also in 2021, the school had fewer interactions with external and foreign partners, resulting in a significant decrease in the number of visits and ceremonies this year. Nevertheless, it was possible to arrange some work visits and international forums at the school. The most important national visits were from the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), the Inspector General of the Armed Forces (IGK), the Commander of the Royal Netherlands Navy Command (C-ZSK), and several directors of the Royal Netherlands Navy Command. 4_KM_Annual_Report_2021_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-18 39 Directorate Personnel and Organization Dutch-Belgian Operational School (NLBEOPS) Commander: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) E.J. Horstman EMSD The year was once again a year full of challenges for NLBEOPS, especially due to the pandemic. The school had already established a robust organization in 2020, which allowed the staff to quickly anticipate the frequent COVID-19 waves this year. The training was adjusted multiple times to the prevailing circumstances and medical challenges. Thanks to good logistical support, internal operations could be maintained. Through the prevailing measures and the consistent use of self-tests, the school significantly reduced the risk of internal infection. A combination of flu-like symptoms and COVID-19 still led to some peaks in temporary staff absence and the necessity to adjust micro-planning. Each department critically and pragmatically assessed operations in relation to teleworking/remote working and the healthy work/life balance.

[Directie Personeel En Bedrijfsvoering (p.18) — narrative]
The personnel filling of NLBEOPS was approximately 85%. The largest personnel shortages were present in the VeVa department, at the Defense Navigation School (DVS), and Above Water Warfare. The personnel situation gradually improved at VeVa. An additional burden for NLBEOPS was the necessary assignment of personnel for deployments and support of the fleet.

[Directie Personeel En Bedrijfsvoering (p.18) — narrative]
Also in 2021, the school had fewer interactions with external and foreign partners, resulting in a significant decrease in the number of visits and ceremonies this year. Nevertheless, it was possible to arrange some work visits and international forums at the school. The most important national visits were from the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), the Inspector General of the Armed Forces (IGK), the Commander of the Royal Netherlands Navy Command (C-ZSK), and several directors of the Royal Netherlands Navy Command. Furthermore, there were visits and participation in training and forums at the school from NATO and European allies.

International training and courses Training and courses at EGUERMIN are not only offered to Dutch and Belgian military personnel but also to those from other NATO partners. These training and courses include components of the binational training, supplemented by the use of the Naval Mine Warfare Gaming System. These courses prepare individuals for the roles of Principal Warfare Officers in Naval Mine Warfare and Staff Officers. Additionally, training is facilitated for personnel within the Naval Coordination and Guidance for Shipping and Allied Warning for Navigation and Information System offices. Wargaming On the wargaming system, members of a Naval Mine Countermeasures staff can plan, execute, and evaluate a mine countermeasure operation. The wargaming system of EGUERMIN is a unique tool within NATO.

Coster At the establishment of the DIB&B in late 2019, it was decided to evaluate after one year to what extent the objectives for the establishment of this directorate have been achieved and what follow-up steps may need to be taken for optimization. This evaluation was conducted from December 2020 to March 2021.

[SECTION BREAK]

In summary, the main conclusions were that the establishment objectives have not yet been achieved. Particularly because there was a lack of clarity regarding the objectives and that the organizational structure of the directorate has not yet been optimally tailored to the tasks. To address these conclusions in practice, a study phase was initiated in September with the aim of reassessing and, where necessary, redefining the tasks and objectives of the directorate as a whole and of the departments individually. The outcome of the study phase is expected by the directorate in 2022.

The Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) Competence Centre CZSK (EC3) assisted with reorganizations in ERP M&F and the introduction of new equipment. The bureau also established the CZSK-wide management of the AKL mutations of the SAP BC codes and conducted various SAP knowledge sessions within CZSK, delivering the CZSK SAP construction manual from input to disposal.

[Directie Personeel En Bedrijfsvoering (p.36) — narrative]
In the operational domain, the Projects Advice and Research bureau contributed to MAROST 2.0, where the Maritime Support tasks not directly related to DMI were transferred to DIB&B, and provided support for the reorganization of the Named Maintenance (BO) support team for Offshore Patrol Vessels (OPVs). Additionally, the bureau produced various evaluation reports, including the evaluation of the newly established DIB&B, the final evaluation of BGO, and the final evaluation of the crew change concept for OPVs. The bureau also contributed to various projects such as Modeling and Simulation, Maritime Cyber Security in the North Sea, and the HR transition of CZSK. In 2021, several new projects were initiated. Among other things, work was done on OKM 2.0, a study on the management of operational data, a study on the deployability of Robotics within CZSK, and an evaluation of the transition from 'Group Leaders to Group Commanders'. 4_KM_Annual_Report_2021_DIRECTORATE_PERSONNEL_AND_OPERATIONS-38 59 Directorate of Integrated Operations and Governance Additionally, the department was responsible for monitoring, coordinating, and extending the various licenses for the applications that are crucial for CZSK's operations. Furthermore, BIVB managed and supported the Narrow Casting System. This system represents the information screens in the various CZSK buildings where important information is presented. The office, specifically the I&I section, developed the new intranet for the entire Defense organization. They also designed a digital registration form, allowing every defense employee to register digitally for various sports activities and to reserve the swimming pool.

[SECTION BREAK]

Change and Innovation Management (V&I) Head: Captain (ktz) D.J.M. Meijer For the development of the Nederdrone Unmanned Aerial Vehicle, V&I signed a new contract with Delft University of Technology. This commitment runs until 2025.

[SECTION BREAK]

The department also ensured the first successful tests of flying on hydrogen (fuel cell). Additionally, the Nederdrone and the self-developed ISD-9 test UAVs participated in the NATO exercise REP(MUS) 2021 in Portugal. In the field of underwater robots, the department carried out two projects. For DDS, a SEASAM underwater robot was purchased to investigate whether this robot can contribute to increasing diving safety during training. Furthermore, V&I successfully experimented in the Caribbean with a simple underwater robot that can inspect the underwater hull. A project team investigated the extent to which digital warfare (CEMA, Cyber and ElectroMagnetic Activities) can be utilized in the maritime domain. The department also initiated research into a replacement for the combat uniform that should provide more wearing comfort and into ways to reduce the infrared signature of marines in the field.

To maintain proficiency in operating in a squadron, the deployments Dutch Defender 21, Eager Hunter 21, Foster Fight, and Hybrid Archer were prepared and executed. During these voyages, MBS provided the Commander Task Group staff that directed the squadron. In the autumn, the staff conducted the deployment Hebrides Archer 2021 in the form of the Commander Amphibious Task Group, including Joint Warrior 21-2. This was the only amphibious exercise of the year and was seen as a stepping stone to Cold Response 22. Despite changes due to COVID-19 issues, Zr.Ms. Evertsen visited many ports. Ultimately, the ship was part of the UKCSG for six months with many unique moments. For instance, it conducted a double RAS with RFA Tidespring and HMS Queen Elizabeth, which was simultaneously launching F-35s. Furthermore, it involved the merging of three Carrier Battle Groups on the eve of the southbound passage through the South China Sea. The most remarkable incidents were the simulated attacks by Russian fighter jets in the Black Sea, in international waters. These aircraft flew dangerously low and close to Zr.Ms. Evertsen, fully armed. After hours of intimidation practices, there were also disruptions to the ship's electronic equipment.

(ltkolmarns) P.C.A.T. van Rooij MSc BBA Joint Arctic Training 21 (JAT21) During JAT21, section 6 and CIS troop 1MCG provided tactical communications in support of safety and command and control. This occurred during the Arctic Movement and Survival Training and Arctic Warfare Training from Camp Orange in Skjold – where an operations room with full functionalities was located – and during the Field Training Exercise in the field through the deployment of the MCG Main Command Post. The Armoured All Terrain Vehicle (AATV) troop of the 24CSS fully participated in JAT21. Since the 14th AATV has been transformed into a Concept Development & Experimentation unit, the 24th AATV supported 1MCG.

[SECTION BREAK]

The Mortar Troop participated in JAT21 this year with twenty marines, including seven novices and thirteen continuations.

[SECTION BREAK]

Among them were three cadre members and a Military Ski Instructor who dedicated themselves to providing the novices with a full training experience and the necessary guidance during the Arctic Movement and Survival Training. Despite the fact that the cadre members had to adjust to the new setup, they experienced teaching, guiding, and coaching under arctic conditions as second nature. Thanks to the extensive experience of our own Military Ski Trainer and MSI, the novices and continuations were well supported during the exercise and the rest of the winter training. This was reflected in the results. All seven newcomers completed the 'novice winter training'. Three of them were allowed to receive the renowned cold weather badge.

[SECTION BREAK]

The primary objective of the FSM was to improve the skills of the Recce Operator and Sniper within the Marine Corps. The secondary objective was to share best practices among the various participants in the exercise.

Due to COVID-19, no foreign units participated in the FSM this year. Combined Exercise 1MCG in Denmark During the combined exercise of 1MCG in Denmark, live firing was included alongside breaching as part of the training in infiltration techniques by Marines from the Assault Engineers, in order to maintain their skills and learn new techniques. Marines moved across the training area Mauken on skis.

[SECTION BREAK]

Operations Directorate Joint Warrior 2021 (JW21) 11 Raiding Squadron (11RSQN) participated in the exercise JW21 in September. JW21 was a large-scale, international naval/amphibious exercise. 11 RSQN consisted of two of its own troops for this exercise. The third troop was from the German Seebataillon. 11RSQN had just been formed after the summer leave, so this was the first time that the relatively inexperienced unit would operate in the amphibious domain.

[SECTION BREAK]

The 24th AATV was stationed under the 14th CSSQN from September 13 to October 23 and had accompanied 1MCG to Great Britain for JW21 and subsequently for the Live Fire Tactical Training at Otterburn. 12RSQN in 29 Palms; Desert Training in California 12RSQN departed on October 2 to 29 Palms, Camp Wilson in the United States. There, a camp in the Middle East was simulated from which various training and scenarios could be conducted. From here, the unit operated for two months, during which each troop had its own departure with stretchers available. Javelin Platoon Commanders Course (Javelin PC) The Javelin PC is a nine-week training course in British Warminster, where the Specialist Weapons School is located.

[SECTION BREAK]

Prior to these nine weeks, a ten-day quarantine was mandatory. This took place in an Airbnb and provided time and opportunities to dive back into the course material and thus start the training well-prepared. At the start of the training, it was immediately clear that due to COVID-19 measures, the trainees were not allowed to leave the barracks for nine weeks.

UAS operators The Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) section of the 15 Reconnaissance, Surveillance and Target Acquisition Squadron (RSTA SQN) is regularly requested for support in the context of ICMS. This often involves support for the police. This can range from assisting in an arrest to flying over urban areas with car fires or as crowd control during a festival. A composite UAS Section from the Marine Corps and Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition & Reconnaissance Command (part of CLAS) conducted UAS operations from June 7 to June 11 from Zr.Ms. Friesland. During this period, the so-called Cruise Voyage took place for the RMN, and the section had the opportunity to conduct maritime UAS-

[SECTION BREAK]

5_KM_Annual_Report_2021_OPERATIONS_DIRECTORATE-22 81 Operations Directorate training to be conducted.

[SECTION BREAK]

In the past, various drones, particularly the PUMA, have been flown from ships of the Royal Netherlands Navy (KM). During Joint Warrior, the UAS Section worked closely with a team from the Recce Sniper Troop. The UAS operators collaborated with the Recce operators to explore how they could work together more effectively in gathering information. By deploying UAS operators alongside the Recce operator and utilizing the 'live-feed data' obtained, Recce operators can sometimes position themselves in a less vulnerable manner. Additionally, the UAS systems can generate images more easily, which Recce operators would otherwise have to work harder to obtain. This could include images behind buildings or highly zoomed-in images within a building to ascertain what is happening there.

[SECTION BREAK]

Joint Warrior was an educational exercise and contributed to further experience building regarding the deployment of UAS in the maritime and amphibious domain and a first collaboration between UAS and Recce operators. Marines were deployed from Zr.Ms. Rotterdam during the final exercise off the coast of Noordwijk.

This is relevant for any potential future participation, as this is currently no longer provided by the MTC. Snake Bite The activities of the CSS SQN in recent years have primarily focused on facilitating 'white' logistics: supporting exercises in a non-tactical setting. However, as American WWII General Dwight Eisenhower once said: 'You will not find it difficult to prove that battles, campaigns and even wars have been lost primarily because of logistics.' Adequate logistical support requires agility, especially in a tactical setting. With this mindset, 20 CSS SQN practiced combat logistics in March at Leusderheide and Marnewaard during Snake Bite. Caribbean Urban Warrior 2021 (CUW) CUW is an annual training of 32RSQ from Aruba, the Detachment Sint-Maarten, and a collaboration with 2nd Marine Recon of the 2 Marine Expeditionary Force at Camp Lejeune in North Carolina. To maximize the capabilities of the available training locations, vehicles, helicopters, and aircraft, two Tactical Air Control Parties were flown in. These consist of a Joint Terminal Attack Controller and a laser operator from a Fire Support Team. Together with a UAS team, in this case a corporal and a marine, they coordinated the (assigned) Surveillance, Target Acquisition, and Reconnaissance capacity within the exercise.

[SECTION BREAK]

Due to the COVID-19 measures in effect at that time, the authorities of the United States imposed a ten-day home quarantine, from which the unit flew by charter to South Carolina. The quarantine took place in Curaçao. After that, and following a negative PCR test, the unit flew via Aruba and Sint-Maarten to pick up 32RSQN and then the detachment.

[SECTION BREAK]

Joint Mountain Training 2021 (JMT21) A lot of work to be done during the last half year of the training year, which concluded with JMT21 from Bardufoss, Norway. Unlike previous years, the certification of a trained RSQ was this time combined with the JMT. Enablers from the CSSQN operated from the base with vehicles. Also during the JMT this fall, much attention was paid to this in collaboration with mobility trainers from MTC.

As part of the national task within NLMARSOF, the minister gained more insight into the operational field of NLMARSOF as the Marine Intervention Unit within the service. text:
Evacuation Afghanistan On Monday afternoon, August 16, the operators of the Non-Foreseeable Special Operation section of C-Squadron were ordered to cut short their summer leave and report as soon as possible to the Nieuwe Haven in Den Helder. There, the entire equipment of the unit was packed and ready for action abroad. Upon arrival at the marsofterrein there, the marines learned that they would fly to Kabul together with two KCT teams and a BSB team to assist in the evacuation of Dutch citizens and status holders. Once landed at Kabul airport, the operators found themselves in a chaotic situation. Within the Dutch task unit, the NLMARSOF section was responsible for securing the flights between Kabul and Islamabad. Ultimately, the task unit facilitated approximately 2,500 people to safety via 21 Dutch evacuation flights, including more than thirty interpreters and their families. With the last C-130 flight to Islamabad on August 26, nearly twenty years of Dutch military presence in Afghanistan came to an end. NLMARSOF operators contributed to this since the first deployment of Taskgroup Orange in 2005.

[SECTION BREAK]

Operators of NLMARSOF exit a Cougar helicopter during the exercise Port Defender in the port of Rotterdam.

[SECTION BREAK]

5_KM_Annual_Report_2021_OPERATIONS_DIRECTORATE-28 87 Operations Directorate Seabased Support Group (SSG) Commander: Major (majmarns) A. Roedoe In the past year, SSG provided second-line logistics for a challenging Operational Joint Task (OJP) and various urgent deployments of Operational Marine Units (OPEMARNS). The fall of Kabul on August 15 resulted in the activation of NLMARSOF and the Marine Spearhead Task Unit, which led elements of SSG to work on issuing the necessary equipment and providing the associated services. The fall of Kabul had a significant impact on the department. Additionally, various units of OPEMARNS specifically called upon specialists from SSG to support them worldwide. Also, in the context of Force Design, members of the units were deployed to further develop logistics. This included specialists such as supply and ammunition managers, armaments technicians, automotive mechanics, and communications personnel.

text: Surface Assault and Training Group (SATG) Commander: Lieutenant Colonel (ltkolmarns) W.F.J. Ramakers MA First Landing Craft Task Unit (LCTU-1) LCTU-1 was the operationally ready unit in 2021 and was therefore scheduled to carry out the Joint Assault Training (JAT). Despite various training sessions being canceled due to the pandemic, the unit executed the training and managed to maintain readiness through various training supports. Since 1MCG conducted the JAT from Skjold, it was also the SATG's wish to work closer to that training area. The location Olavsvern is a former submarine base owned by the Norwegian Wilhelmsen Governmental Services, and this organization was very willing to rent the accommodation to SATG. The Mine Service group includes the Mine Counter Measures (MCM) operational staff, DDG, the MCM Module Group (MMG), Zr.Ms. Makkum, Zr.Ms. Schiedam, Zr.Ms. Urk, Zr.Ms. Vlaardingen, Zr.Ms. Willemstad, and Zr.Ms. Zierikzee, as well as two hydrographic survey vessels: Zr.Ms. Luymes and Zr.Ms. Snellius.

[SECTION BREAK]

Not only did crews have to quarantine before departure, but the number of port visits could be described as 'meager.' The submarines trained both in Scandinavian waters and in the Mediterranean Sea. de Wit No contribution received. Naval Aviation Service (MLD) Group Senior: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) N. Kleingeld SSCG At the beginning of 2021, the MLD faced an unplanned challenge. Due to technical malfunctions on Zr.Ms. Groningen, there were only two trips to the Caribbean instead of the planned three. Despite this setback, SSCG-9 and 10 proved to be very successful. Together, they intercepted an impressive total of 11,626 kilograms of cocaine on various drug routes. An NH90 takes off from the Maritime Airbase De Kooy with two dummy torpedoes.

[SECTION BREAK]

5_KM_Annual_Report_2021_OPERATIONS_DIRECTORATE-34 93 Operations Directorate SNMG In the last four months of the year, the MLD supported the SNMG on Zr.Ms. Van Amstel with an NH90. Exercises In 2021, the service participated in several important exercises, including NOST & Joint Warrior, during which the MLD enhanced readiness and cooperation skills. Another exercise was Joint Warrior Amphibious. This was an intensive exercise focused on amphibious operations, during which the amphibious flight (Flight 2) embarked for the first time. A crucial exercise was FOST Culdrose, to ensure combat readiness and interoperability. Additionally, the MLD conducted an exercise focused on anti-submarine warfare: ASW Hyeres. In this, the service practiced improving the capability to address submarine threats, even in a deep-water environment. There were also five Helicopter Qualification weeks this year, of which two were big deck and three were small deck.

[SECTION BREAK]

Maritime Warfare Centre (MWC) Head: Captain (ktz) H. Welmer, from January 21 Colonel (ltkolmarns) J. de Wolf Throughout the year, the prospect of vaccination came into view, thus providing a way out of the situation of limited operational capabilities. Notable new restrictions due to COVID-19 included quarantines for sailing periods. The MWC provides seariders for operational units, and they had to quarantine before deployment under ever-changing regimes. An unwanted effect of this was that instead of being away from their workplace for a few days, they were now absent for several weeks. All annual NATO and multinational meetings were, of course, virtual, which did mean they took much less time, but also that they yielded much less.

Response to the Corona pandemic Since Monday, March 16, 2020, the staff of HYD worked from home as much as possible, and several other measures were in place.

[SECTION BREAK]

The specific application at the service was carried out by the Chief Hydrographer with input from the MT members, based on instructions from the Central Expertise Center for Working Conditions and Health, CZSK, and the garrison commander. Due to operational responsibilities, HYD was granted the status of vital. Cold conditions on board Zr.Ms. De Zeven Provinciën in British waters with a view of a Royal Navy frigate.

[SECTION BREAK]

5_KM_Annual_Report_2021_OPERATIONS_DIRECTORATE-38 97 Operations Directorate organization. This meant that “where working from home is not possible (…) work in the office is allowed within the condition that the COVID-19 measures have been implemented.” Offer Development The International Hydrographic Organization (IHO) developed new standards for the accessibility of hydrographic data, based on S-100, the Universal Hydrographic Data Model. HYD made an active contribution to this, including taking the lead in writing the guidelines for following the Worldwide Electronic Navigational Products Database for S-100 Principles. The transition to S-100 and S-100-based product specifications was initiated with the adoption of the S-100 Roadmap during the second IHO Assembly under Dutch chairmanship. The Roadmap is evaluated annually in the IHO Council, in which the Netherlands has been elected. At the Dutch initiative, the second Assembly indicated to the Council for the period 2020-2023 the theme “the effective implementation of the Revised Strategic Plan keeping in mind to apply the principles of ISO9001.” The fifth Council then decided that “ISO9001 principles will be experimented on the development of the Product Specification for ENCs, S-101 ed. 2.0.0.” The first steps for S-100 implementation at HYD have now been taken, with the production of test datasets for three different standards. The service shared the first results internationally, for which it received much appreciation.

text:
The licensing fee has been significantly reduced to stimulate demand, particularly for nautical apps. Private publishers of nautical products without a license or with a virtually inactive license are being approached for a license at the new rate.

[SECTION BREAK]

Demand Development The trend of a decrease in paper products in favor of digital products (2014-2019) has changed into a stable situation. In absolute terms, the sales of paper and digital products gradually returned to the level before the COVID-19 measures. The trend of licensed products to the use of the nautical products themselves (2014-2017) has stabilized for several years (2017-2021). Reuse via INSPIRE showed a mixed picture. Reuse via EMODnet, and thus the total sales, showed significant growth, particularly in the bathymetric view service.

[SECTION BREAK]

5_KM_Annual_Report_2021_OPERATIONS_DIRECTORATE-39 98 Operations Directorate Renewal of Distribution Channels The International Center for ENCs (IC-ENC), where the Chief Hydrographer (Chef der Hydrografie) played an important role as chair of the Steering Group, prepared for the distribution of S-100 series products. In this context, the distribution of ENCs (S-57 and S-101) was also redesigned. The reuse under license of ENC data via IC-ENC is a desire of many license holders. IC-ENC began operational use of the non-ECDIS service. However, the number of license holders is still limited. The Distribution Working Group attempted to eliminate the reported reasons for this, where possible.

[SECTION BREAK]

The new OneOcean defense contract for the provision of nautical products has been successfully made operational for all operational units, and the new procedures have been implemented in Instruction CZSK DOPS HYD 001.

[SECTION BREAK]

A so-called VIR E&E analysis indicated a security level for the system TBB-4 and for the data Departmental Confidential. ICT Developments In 2021, a permanent ICT budget was finally allocated to the service. This rectified an error from the reorganization of 2013. Hydrographic measuring instruments are being launched.

text:
The personnel of the establishment found a good balance for hybrid working. Tugboat Waddenzee in the New Harbor. To the left are Zr.Ms. Karel Doorman and Zr.Ms. Rotterdam docked.

[SECTION BREAK]

Directorate of Material Maintenance The new construction plans for the revitalized barracks progressed steadily, and the detailed allocation of units was developed last year in a so-called area plan. This made it clear what is coming and what it will look like. Gradually, more defined outlines emerged, and artistic impressions were created that provided a good picture. The negotiations and discussions with the municipality proceeded smoothly, and throughout the year, the municipality presented a note of principles for the entire area in which the plans for the part to be transferred are recorded.

[SECTION BREAK]

While construction workers were renovating the police station on Lijnbaansgracht, the Jordaan team of the Amsterdam police unit has been based in building 012 since the autumn. Team Amstel was already located in this building. The consequence of all this police presence on the site is that a portacabin complex was set up for building 014 because the police do not have sufficient changing facilities in building 012. Events and activities in 2020 This year, various events were again on the calendar, but the cancellations affected VeVa students in Amsterdam.

[SECTION BREAK]

The Directorate of Materiel Maintenance continued to receive requests, and most major events were significantly reduced or completely canceled. The effects of the global pandemic continued to dictate everything this year. The entire annual planning changed almost monthly. After each COVID-19 press conference, it was back to the drawing board to see what was possible and what was not. The staff made the event center completely COVID-19 compliant, allowing meetings and small conferences to take place in a scaled-down format with plenty of spacing. Major events such as the Canal Pride and Amsterdam City Swim were canceled for the second year in a row, and the Sinterklaas arrival was carried out in a completely adjusted form. The fact that the pandemic would last over a year and that the events sector would remain inactive came as a surprise. Business operations also remained on a low burner this year, but at the same time, the COVID-19 crisis provided an opportunity to carry out significant overdue maintenance in and around the Event Center Amsterdam. The transformation of this building, initiated in 2020, continued this year, and the finishing touches were realized.

The staff made the event center completely COVID-19 compliant, allowing meetings and small conferences to take place in a scaled-down format with plenty of spacing. Major events such as the Canal Pride and Amsterdam City Swim were canceled for the second year in a row, and the Sinterklaas arrival was carried out in a completely adjusted form. The fact that the pandemic would last over a year and that the events sector would remain inactive came as a surprise. Business operations also remained on a low burner this year, but at the same time, the COVID-19 crisis provided an opportunity to carry out significant overdue maintenance in and around the Event Center Amsterdam. The transformation of this building, initiated in 2020, continued this year, and the finishing touches were realized.

text: Directorate of Material Maintenance Naval Training Vessel Van Kinsbergen The MOV Van Kinsbergen is used for nautical practical training. The ship has been specially built and equipped for this purpose. It accommodates sixteen trainees. Navigation and Training Bridge The Van Kinsbergen has, in addition to the regular navigation bridge, a fully equipped secondary training bridge. The ship is suitable for practicing all navigation procedures and safe mooring and unmooring. Deployment Annually, Van Kinsbergen sails approximately 200 days. The main user is the KIM (Royal Netherlands Naval College). The ship is deployed to teach future naval officers (adelborsten) practical nautical skills. These skills are necessary to work as a watch officer on the bridge of a naval ship. The ship serves as a supplement to theory and (bridge) simulator lessons. Thus, future navigation officers receive various training on board, such as mooring and unmooring. Additionally, the ship also has a formative function, including team building and character development.

After that, from March 14 to March 19, the ship went to sea for the Maritime Institute Willem Barentsz (MIWB). The Van Kinsbergen conducted day trips with the students to familiarize them with working on board a ship.

[SECTION BREAK]

6_KM_Annual_Report_2021_MATERIAL_MAINTENANCE-18 119 Directorate of Material Maintenance of the ship. The students participated in various components including watchkeeping on the Bridge, in the Engine Room, and on deck. The Van Kinsbergen docked at West Terschelling during this week. From March 24 to March 31, the ship sailed for DVS, for the ZWST-Klein Bovenwater course with Middelfart as a stopover port. This was followed by a second practical sailing period for the cadets, from April 22 to May 27. Subsequently, there was a week of sailing for the horizontal short-term entrants of the Higher Nautical Education. From June 18 to July 16, the last sailing practice week took place for the students before they go on Company Introduction. During this time, the students determine the Weekly Practice Program with various exercises and routes.

[SECTION BREAK]

Only the port visits are determined by the permanent crew. This is the opportunity for the students to demonstrate their capabilities, and the crew and instructors take a step back, intervening only when absolutely necessary.

text:
Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean is focused on countering drug trafficking by sea. CZMCARIB promotes regional security and stability by, among other things, conducting counter illicit trafficking operations and through international military cooperation. The United States and France are the main international partners in this effort.

[SECTION BREAK]

C-ZMCARIB fulfills the CIT task as Commander Task Group 4.4 (CTG 4.4), a subordinate commander of the American Joint Interagency Task Force South. The support of civil authorities is also a priority. The Dutch Armed Forces have developed into a structural security partner within the Kingdom. With its highly developed specialist and unique capabilities, the armed forces now offer broader support options. CZMCARIB provides units that can be deployed for military assistance to Aruba, Curaçao, Sint Maarten, and the BES islands. CZMCARIB also provides support to third parties, primarily to the Coast Guard in the Caribbean (KWCARIB). C-ZMCARIB is also the Director of KWCARIB.

[SECTION BREAK]

It also provides emergency assistance during disasters and crises. Finally, CZMCARIB supports the Social Development Programs in Curaçao and Aruba. Zr.Ms. Holland and a FRISC were deployed off the coast of Haiti.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Area Vision In order to realize the mission of CZMCARIB as adequately as possible in light of the surrounding changes, a vision has been established. The vision of CZMCARIB is: ‘CZMCARIB is the relevant maritime and security partner in the Caribbean, as part of the CZSK’. This means that CZMCARIB aims to be recognized as the obvious and reliable partner when it comes to contributing to security in the Caribbean part of the Kingdom. ‘Relevant maritime’ and ‘security partner’ in the above vision refers to the fact that CZMCARIB assigns a high priority to the second and third core tasks.

text:
Due to national and international agreements, it wants to promote the international and local rule of law with its own resources, for example by contributing capabilities to (inter)national organizations or by providing military assistance. With these own resources, it can be deployed for many diverse scenarios to support civil authorities, for example for conducting searches, tracking, diving units, observation, and emergency assistance. CZMCARIB does this in good cooperation with national and international partners in the security chain.

[SECTION BREAK]

Reflection on 2021 Just like in 2020, COVID-19 also dominated this year. The pandemic had a significant impact on the operations of CZMCARIB as well as its operational activities. Local authorities, particularly from Curaçao, regularly called upon military assistance to support them with COVID-19 related activities. International Drug Enforcement In addition to the external defense of six islands of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in the Caribbean, the Defense plays an important role in maintaining the international rule of law in the Caribbean area. Given the location of the islands, this primarily involves combating international drug trafficking by sea. The Navy in the Caribbean is thus closely integrated into the international drug enforcement organization Joint Interagency Task Force South based in Key West. The Commander (kltz) of the Navy in the Caribbean is therefore the commander of Task Group 4.4, one of the task groups of this organization.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Navy in the Caribbean The task assigned to CZMCARIB from the Land Packages is to professionalize the Caribbean military, including modernizing the legal position and (re)establishing the Social Development Program for disadvantaged youth in both Aruba and Curaçao. Throughout the year, the department began drafting the CZMCARIB Ambition Document. This document looks ten years ahead and describes both the ambition in terms of personnel and equipment. The goal is to complete the Ambition Document in 2022 and formally present it to C-ZSK.

[SECTION BREAK]

Despite COVID-19, CMCARIB made a strong effort to expand the CARIB training hub. For example, work was done on a Forward Operating Base at the Wacawa training area in Curaçao and on a training village for Urban Operations at the Marine Barracks Savaneta in Aruba. In 2021, CZMCARIB took the first steps to pay extra attention to real estate in the area.

text:
The SSCG was equipped with an NH90 onboard helicopter. In addition to the usual deployment for KWCARIB and CTG 4.4, the SSCG contributed to emergency assistance in Haiti. This was in response to the severe earthquake that struck the country on August 14. From August 19 to September 2, the SSCG distributed, among other things, 35,000 liters of water and 25,000 kg of goods in the hard-to-reach affected areas for Netherlands Task Force Haiti. The Task Force consisted of the MHKC, SSCG, Marine Squadron CARIB (MSC), the Boat Platoon, Company in the West (CIDW), and EGB.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean Counter Drugs Zr.Ms. Holland patrolled during its period of presence both for KWCARIB and for CTG 4.4, with several successful seizures. In collaboration with international units, approximately 10,200 kg and 1,900 kg of contraband were removed from the trade market in 2021 by CTG 4.4 and KWCARIB, respectively, through confiscation. These international operations were carried out by the ship with various countries such as the United States, France, Colombia, and the United Kingdom.

[SECTION BREAK]

Hurricane Relief Assistance Where in 2020 COVID-19 disrupted plans, the Hurricane Relief Exercise (HUREX) took place in 2021 in preparation for the hurricane season. From May 26 to June 5, rehearsals were conducted in the Windward Islands for the hurricane season, which runs from June 1 to November 30. During the exercise, MHKC worked closely with local authorities and aid organizations to ensure smooth cooperation during the hurricane season. Land Units The MSC, rotations of the CIDW, and the Marine detachment in Sint Maarten were limited in their readiness activities due to the overcrowded ICUs in the countries.

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean was temporarily unable to conduct risky activities. Where possible, the regular training program continued to ensure readiness for deployment, which was sufficiently addressed in 2021. In particular, the authorities in Curaçao frequently called upon the Curaçao Militia (CURMIL) and CIDW for assistance. The CIDW search team was successfully deployed multiple times in Curaçao and Bonaire.

[SECTION BREAK]

The MSC provided the Maritime Intermediate Guard Team to the SSCG for the last time in 2021. Furthermore, after the interruption last year, the annual exercise of the MSC, Caribbean Urban Warrior, was able to take place again in the United States (Camp LeJeune). Military Assistance In 2021, CZMCARIB provided 28 soft and hard military assistance operations to the authorities of the countries and islands of the Kingdom. From February to June, the EGB opened a vaccination site at Marine Base Parera.

[SECTION BREAK]

The EODD was called into action twice in Curaçao to destroy ammunition, fireworks, and explosive materials. In Bonaire and Curaçao, the search team provided assistance during searches of

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Navy in the Caribbean seized prisons, residences, plots, and vehicles. Among other things, they found phones, money, drugs, and documents.

[SECTION BREAK]

On Saba, the Sint Maarten Detachment (DETSXM) supported the KNMI in the installation of a new weather station. MSC established static observation posts in Aruba to support KWCARIB, focusing on illegal landings due to the deteriorating situation in Venezuela. In Curaçao, CURMIL provided hard military assistance in enforcing COVID-19 measures, including the curfew. In September, CURMIL supported the Curaçao Police Corps in setting up traffic controls aimed at intercepting firearms. A safe house was established at Marine Base Parera to support the Curaçao Police Corps during important hearings.

[SECTION BREAK]

Visiting units Due to travel restrictions, most visiting units had to be canceled in the first half of the year. Despite the limited remaining period, Army personnel unpacked a package of water bottles delivered by an NH90 for the local population.

Command of the Navy in the Caribbean, among other Dutch units such as the 41st Armored Engineer Battalion, NLMARSOF, DDS, 45th Armored Infantry Battalion, Corps Commando Troops, 101st Engineer Battalion, and MOC, as well as foreign units from the United States Marine Corps, can make use of the CARIB Training Hub. Director of Control: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) ing. P. Borsje-Senders. In 2021, the Control Department of CZMCARIB worked to support C-ZMCARIB in the preparation, execution, progress, and quality of financial policy advice. It also compiled the budget, established the spending program, and provided management and steering reports. Finance: In 2021, CZSK made budget cuts in several areas. In this process, less budget was allocated to the Caribbean than was originally available. CZMCARIB had a budget of 18.7 million euros in 2021. Due to limited travel opportunities caused by the COVID-19 pandemic and the fact that fewer external units conducted exercises in the Caribbean, fewer activities took place. CZMBARIB also organized fewer activities for its own units due to the pandemic. As a result, most foreign exercises were canceled, and units traveled much less between the islands for training.

[SECTION BREAK]

The realization of the budget fell short as a result. Furthermore, the establishment of the Country Package led to a 12.5% reduction in the salaries of local staff.

7_Navy_Annual_Report_2021_COMMAND_OF_THE_NAVY_CARIB-11 130 Command of the Navy in the Caribbean Area Marine Base Parera (MBPAR) Commander: Lieutenant Commander (kltz) R.A.J. Wesdorp MSc The motto of the emblem of MBPAR is 'cheerful and bold'. Two character traits that are characteristic of a good 'host'.

[SECTION BREAK]

The base houses the staff of C-ZMCARIB and the Rescue and Coordination Center of the Caribbean Coast Guard. MBPAR also provides accommodation for a rotating company of the army. They are initially in the Caribbean for a training program. If necessary, they also provide humanitarian assistance, for example after a hurricane or to maintain public order. The company is also deployed for ceremonial tasks, such as at the Opening of the States. This boat group at MBPAR is mainly used to support various operations and exercises. In addition, they can also conduct beach reconnaissance and river operations. The Navy Operations Center is also located at Marine Base Parera. This center directs all counter-drug operations in the Caribbean area. The base has workshops where all floating and rolling material is maintained.

[SECTION BREAK]

The EGB opened a vaccination center at MBPAR, which operated from February to June.

In addition, the Curaçao Police Corps established a safe house on the base for important hearings on the island. Marine Barracks Suffisant (MKSUF) Commander: Major (majmarns) S. Baan MKSUF was the scene of the Maximus trial this year, where the barracks organization and its security partners set a new standard for multidisciplinary security and facilitation of administrative events in the Caribbean area. This garnered significant international media attention and the influx of new CURMIL increased as a result. Consequently, the barracks was able to carry out extensive renovations of the barracks, company restaurant, and classrooms. In addition, the shooters from Suffisant won the rotating trophy from the Contact of Former and Active Serving Marines (COM) and MKSUF laid the first preparations.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean opened the CURMIL to women, which had not been possible before. The HRM organization of the Local Personnel was made independent to strengthen the synergy between the employees of the Netherlands and Curaçao. The annual captains' dinner also took place, and small groups worked within the guidelines on local initiatives such as activities with nursing homes and schools.

Marine Barracks Savaneta Aruba (MSKSAV) Commander: Lieutenant Colonel (ltkolmarns) B. van Beekhuizen Marine Barracks Savaneta is located in Aruba and houses the 32nd Marine Squadron (32RSQN) and the Aruban Militia.

[SECTION BREAK]

These consist of a staff, platoons, and supporting units. The Marine Squadron and the Aruban Militia (ARUMIL) have various tasks. For this, they train and exercise in the United States, French Guiana, Suriname, French Caribbean islands, and the Windward and Leeward Islands. A platoon of the Aruban militia guards and secures the barracks. Zr.Ms. Holland is moored in the harbor as a station ship.

Commandement der Zeemacht in het Caribisch Gebied Marine Steunpunt Point Blanche (MSTPPB) Commandant: Major (majmarns) A. Noordam Over the past year, MSTPPB strengthened its relationships with the Emergency Operation Center (EOC), which is represented by various ministries. DETSXM also engaged with the EOC, contributing to a Table Top training for disaster preparedness, among other activities. Within the Emergency Support Function 5 (ESF5), the body that represents all safety partners in Sint Maarten, ties were also strengthened. At least once a quarter, the EOC and ESF 5 team met to discuss their needs. This resulted in improved cooperation plans for providing potential military assistance. Throughout the year, plans for the construction of the new Marine Support Point began to take shape. The parties involved signed the leasehold contract, and recently the national government real estate company outlined a preliminary sketch of the barracks.

[SECTION BREAK]

Military Assistance During the 2021 hurricane season, DETSXM provided military assistance at the request of the government of Sint Maarten in close cooperation with the Sint Maarten Police Corps.

Support vessel Zr.Ms. Pelikaan Commander: Lieutenant (ltz1) D.M. Boom, from March 26 Lieutenant (ltz1) M.J.C. Jereskes.

[SECTION BREAK]

The year was the first fully operational year after the MLU for Zr.Ms. Pelikaan, which had been away from the operational area for nearly a year. The pandemic also impacted the operational program and limited the ship's freedom regarding port visits. Normally, the crew would carry out the annual maintenance in January and February. This year, however, that took place in March and April. Therefore, Zr.Ms. Kustwacht patrolled off the coast of Philipsburg.

[SECTION BREAK]

Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean initiated the transport of CIDW to Aruba and MSC to Curaçao in January. In February, the ship utilized the operational area for internal training for one and a half weeks. Due to the risk of COVID-19 infections and the complexity of testing, it was decided not to conduct a rest and recreation port visit. In March, the annual maintenance began, during which the crew prepared the ship for the hurricane season. This process was hampered by a strict lockdown in Curaçao, requiring personnel to work from home or take leave. Fortunately, the overall impact remained small, except for a few specialists from DMI who could not come.

[SECTION BREAK]

During the maintenance on March 26, the command transfer took place, with Lieutenant Commander (kltz) D.M. Boom handing over command to Lieutenant Commander (kltz) M.J.C. Jereskes.

[SECTION BREAK]

After approval from the classification bureau Lloyds and the material seaworthiness authority, the ship was again full mission capable in May and commenced with several transport assignments of equipment between Curaçao and Aruba and CIDW between Curaçao and Bonaire. At the beginning of June, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan conducted the annual HUREX as a dress rehearsal for deployment during the hurricane season. In Sint Maarten, the ship made use of Zr.Ms. Pelikaan in Curaçao.

text:
Command of the Naval Forces in the Caribbean provided the crew with the opportunity to train in the main deployment: transporting large quantities of cargo, conducting hydrographic surveys of the port, logistically facilitating colleagues stationed on land (in accordance with the shit, shave and shower routine), and supplying water and fuel. Additionally, a reconnaissance was conducted for the new crew members on Sint Maarten, focusing on locations that play an important role during deployments (airport, hospital, headquarters, etc.). With the completion of HUREX, Zr.Ms. Pelikaan was ready for deployment with a notice to move of 48 hours, allowing the ship to arrive in the disaster area within hours after the passage of a hurricane. After HUREX, the ship collaborated for several days with the boat platoon in Curaçao, providing amphibious support to T-squadron, a training unit of NLMARSOF. In June, internal preparations were again made, and a port visit to Aruba was conducted as part of rest and recreation. After a five-week leave, the crew worked under the leadership of MOST during a two-week CT. Due to COVID-19, the leadership decided not to conduct a port visit due to the significant impact a potential infection could have on the training program. In September, the ship participated in the annual exercise Windward Express, where it executed a training program on Sint Maarten for two troops from the MSC of Aruba. The focus of the exercise was on amphibious operations and optimizing cooperation between Zr.Ms. Pelikaan and the MSC.

[SECTION BREAK]

In October, the ship supported the DDG, where the very shallow water team received logistical assistance on the west coast of Aruba and the deep dive team in Caracas Bay in Curaçao. Due to an incoming request, the ship was able to provide support on relatively short notice in November for renewing military cooperation with Suriname surrounding the Surinamese independence celebration. For this purpose, two Surinamese officers flew to Curaçao for a four-week military exchange.

text:
This was the second year in which COVID-19 played a restrictive role, but the situation normalized during 2021, allowing for more regular opportunities to carry out the work.

[SECTION BREAK]

For instance, the service resumed work visits to Bonaire, where the KMar is active, and to Sint Maarten to be more accessible to personnel and their families on these islands. After the emergency aid to Haiti, the department provided aftercare for the units that were deployed. In addition to the regular BMW support for employees and their families, activities for post-active veterans resumed in 2021. In Curaçao, the Veterans Association Curaçao was active and represents the interests of veterans residing on the island. BMW was in contact with this association to provide access for veterans living in Curaçao and Aruba from the position as a partner within the National Care System for Veterans. On both islands, various assistance contacts with post-active veterans were established. As part of veteran care, the service also maintained contact with the Veterans Care Desk of the General Civil Pension Fund in the Netherlands.

[SECTION BREAK]

Medical Service CZMCARIB Head: Captain (ktz) R.J. Joosten The Primary Health Care Company (EGB) and the Defense Dental Service provide primary care in the Caribbean part of the Kingdom from the Health Center Curaçao. Additionally, there is a branch at the location in Aruba. At both centers, they provide integrated care to military personnel and deployed Dutch civilian employees. The Dental Service and EGB in the CARIB also provide 24/7 care to the accompanying family members of the deployed employees. Furthermore, the staff of the EGB provides operational support to the MHKC.

The renewal and modernization of the Coast Guard is taking more shape. Not only has progress been made in the ICT part of the Maritime Operations Center project, but in 2021, the architect and project management were selected for the new construction, an important step towards the realization of the new operations center. Intensive work has been done with the commissioning parties of the Coast Guard and the Rijksrederij to find a solution for the implementation of the 24/7 enforcement concept with the existing vessels. An important development in the tasks of the Coast Guard is the intensification of tasks to ensure shipping safety in the context of offshore wind energy. The ongoing construction of wind farms in the North Sea requires additional monitoring of shipping. To this end, an extra desk has been set up at the CCC, additional personnel have been recruited, and since 2021, one additional Emergency Recovery & Towing Vessel has been patrolling in the southern North Sea. For the influx of personnel, a limited reorganization process was completed in 2021. Progress has been made in the development of the internal organization of the Coast Guard due to the influx of new personnel in previous years, both in operational and supporting processes. This is particularly visible in the crisis organization, structuring functional ICT management, implementing GDPR legislation, documenting processes, and renewing operational agreements with partner services.

FOREWORD In your hands, you have the Yearbook of the Royal Netherlands Navy 2022. In this, you can read about the deployments the navy undertook during extensive international operations and exercises, as well as the actions taken by the shore organization to facilitate these deployments. Although some COVID-19 measures were still in place at the beginning of the year, the government gradually lifted these restrictions, allowing for more activities. Thus, exercises and events could continue, and normalcy returned. The Royal Netherlands Navy (KM) once again made a significant impression during the Navy Days in Den Helder. Additionally, this year saw Velas Latinoamérica Curaçao, a unique celebration featuring several tall ships visiting Willemstad.

[SECTION BREAK]

The KM was also represented there. With many visitors, it was a great success and a wonderful opportunity to showcase what the KM has to offer. The personnel underwent many new trainings, courses, and participated in (international) exercises. At the World Port Days in Rotterdam, the navy was present with marines and ships to introduce visitors to the naval forces.

The resources promised in the coalition agreement and in the measures note starting from 2023 and subsequent years had a positive effect on the implementation of the plans in 2022. Due to national and global shortages of goods and services and tightness in the labor market, production capacity at C-ZSK still lagged behind in 2022.

Organizational overviews in relation to necessary capacity. Organizational Overviews In 2022, CZSK (Royal Netherlands Navy Command) spent a net € 101 million more on personnel expenses than was included in the draft budget. The cause of this is primarily due to additional expenses resulting from the collective labor agreement 2021-2023, temporary salary structure allowances, and increased compensation for pension costs. Due to underfilling of permanent staff, expenditures for hiring temporary workers and consultants for operational management and IT were higher than anticipated. This hiring was necessary to procure essential personnel in order to prevent stagnation in the execution of the Navy's tasks as much as possible.

[SECTION BREAK]

In 2022, CZSK received € 3.3 million more in the operational budget than was included in the draft budget. This was mainly caused by a higher contribution from the countries to the Caribbean Coast Guard (catching up on backlog) from previous years. Defense Materiel Fund (DMF) In the DMF, expenditures in 2022 were higher than the budget allocated at the beginning of the year (€ 155 million) plus additional allocations (€ 97 million). However, due to a budget (€ 83 million) being deferred to 2026 through a cash shift, a surplus of € 33 million was presented as of December 31.

[SECTION BREAK]

This is mainly due to a higher reliability of delivery of goods and services than was estimated at the time of the cash shift, resulting in more being realized. The budget shifted to 2026 can be used to cover potential future shortfalls in the DMF. Additionally, within the fund in 2022, € 13.4 million more was received due to extra efforts in collecting overdue invoices. This includes CZSK catching up from previous years (e.g., maintenance on Portuguese M-frigates) and, in net terms, higher incidental VAT receipts. These extra receipts are and will be used for the maintenance of maritime materiel.

For 2022, the focal points of the directorate were: Improving the space for tailored agreements, where protocols are guiding but not leading. Developing opportunities for additional capacity such as alternative recruitment and flexible use of labor market potential. Intensifying collaboration with the Personnel Logistics Service Center, the business community, knowledge institutions, the province of North Holland, and employment agencies for the purpose of recruitment. Developing, in addition to a core of well-trained personnel with long-term contracts, a flexible layer by utilizing various contract forms in an open personnel system. Knowledge building and knowledge retention are anchored through career paths and longer job durations.

text:
Schelkers The JUZA department is part of the Directorate Personnel and Organization (DP&O), one of the four line directorates of CZSK. The department advises and supports CZSK, the directors of CZSK, and commanders of units on all legal issues that arise. JUZA provides legal advice and acts as a point of contact for the directors and commanders within CZSK. Additionally, JUZA monitors the legal and administrative diligence of operations within CZSK. The main areas of law that the department deals with include (military) criminal and disciplinary law, operational law, and state and administrative law. These areas of law are organized into three different offices.

[SECTION BREAK]

Thus, every employee at JUZA can serve as the first point of contact (counter function) for questions directed to the department. JUZA does not provide legal advice to individual military personnel but does assist them if necessary. In criminal or disciplinary matters, JUZA is primarily involved on the side of CZSK and Defense as an organization. If a military member is involved in a criminal case, they can receive assistance from Defense in that matter.

[SECTION BREAK]

All of this aims to ensure that CZSK can always rely on sufficient, well-qualified, and well-motivated personnel to carry out its tasks. The P&O department has the following main tasks: providing P&O advice to CZSK regarding the functioning of the personnel function area, the organization and staffing, and the resulting required personnel readiness within CZSK; providing P&O advice to line management, commanders, and heads of service units, thereby achieving a uniform, consistent, and coherent implementation of personnel policy within the given frameworks; organizing and executing management development up to the level of Lieutenant Commander (kltz)/Lieutenant Colonel (ltkol)/scale 13, in conjunction with and aligned to the Management Development (MD) policy for the levels of Captain (ktz)/scale 14 and higher; organizing and executing the job assignment process and personnel management for military personnel within the frameworks of the Flexible Personnel System; organizing and executing career guidance for military personnel within the frameworks of this system and for civilian personnel; organizing and executing demand management; overseeing the various possibilities for the deployment of flexible personnel capacity; managing the intake of returning military personnel and the intake pool of civilian personnel; supporting line management in discussions with participation committees at various levels and promoting participation in general.

text:
D.J.M. Meijer EMSD Bureau Training Needs Assessment & Evaluation (OB&E) OB&E supported the initial phase of a new defense-wide operational management process regarding qualification. The full implementation within CZSK requires considerable preparation, as the CZSK operational management is not set up for this process. Under the leadership of OB&E, this subproject will be realized within the program Developing Training and Education, which started at the end of this year under the direction of OKM. Maritime Simulation Center (SimCenMar) 2022 was characterized for SimCenMar as the year in which two major formal projects commenced, namely Full Warship Trainer for Sea Training Command (STC) and OKM and Navigation Simulator for small vessels (NavSim) for OKM. Both projects involve Steering, Control & Coordination Training Royal Netherlands Navy (SBC-OKM).

[SECTION BREAK]

Directorate of Personnel and Organization finances for development, software and hardware, management and operation. Development was carried out by temporarily appointing project staff and interns (the so-called flexible layer of SimCenMar), managed by the permanent core. Both projects reported to the Program Steering Group. At the Naval Museum, a temporary exhibition titled "Navy Games – more than a game" started at the end of 2022, showcasing how the Navy has historically and currently uses games in training. The prototype of the navigation simulator, built by SimCenMar, allows visitors to experience a game scenario while virtually sailing in a Fast Raiding Interception and Special forces Craft (FRISC). The center signed a cooperation agreement with Damen Schelde Naval Shipbuilding, which aims to collaborate in the development, sharing, and management of capacity and knowledge regarding Extended Reality. The close cooperation with the media colleague in Amsterdam continued in 2022. In addition to facilitating internship placements in the third and fourth years and providing a final assignment for fourth-year students, SimCenMar is now engaging earlier in the curriculum, allowing students to familiarize themselves with the work and guidance of SimCenMar through small assignments. For the center, this is an ideal opportunity to attract the right students for internship positions even earlier.

This includes revising the Defense-wide 'Policy Frameworks O&iT: reconsidered and aligned' issued in 2016 to the 'Policy Frameworks Training & Individual Training (2022)'. The reasons for this were recent (technological) developments, the outcomes of the TNO research program V1806, the implications of the Qualification Chain for Individual Personal Readiness, the validity of the policy, and the implementation agreements until 2020. The main changes in 2022 compared to the policy frameworks from 2016 were: From Just In Time, Just Enough (JITJE, 2016) to Just as needed, Just in time, Just in place (JAN JIT JIP, 2022). From Civil Unless (2016) to Civil Collaboration (2022), Purple Unless (2016) to Joint and Combined (2022).

[SECTION BREAK]

The principle of the didactic concept Professionally Oriented Training (BGO) remains in effect. It remains important that within the BGO concept, the learning environment approaches (or simulates) the professional context and is based on practical examples and varying circumstances.
